الأحاديث النبوية وذكرها في القرآن الكريم: The Prophetic Hadith and Their Mention in the Noble Quran
بكل حديث صحيح آيته ونصه المخرَّج وبيان ا: Each sound hadith with its verse, its sourced text and the link between them in the exegetes' words, in six chapters: the Sunnah in the Quran, Prophetic exegesis, verses the Prophet ﷺ recited, the merit of verses and surahs, hadith on the revelation of verses, and verses in his supplication ﷺ.
الآية بلفظ مصحف المدينة (مجمع الملك فهد): The verse is in the wording of the Madina Mushaf (King Fahd Complex), the hadith is cut verbatim from the bundled Six Books with its source and number, with its grade from the two Sahihs or, for the Sunan, from the data source; the exegete's words are quoted verbatim from the bundled tafsirs. The titles and the explanation of the connection are brief wording based on the hadith and the exegete's statement, and this section contains no weak hadith.
الصلة بين الحديث والآية: How the hadith connects to the verse
آيات أمر الله فيها بطاعة رسوله ﷺ واتباعه: Verses in which Allah commands obedience to His Messenger ﷺ, following him and referring judgment to him, and states that explaining the revelation is part of his mission and that what he speaks is revelation. Each verse is paired with a sound hadith on its meaning and a quotation from the exegetes on how it proves the authority of the Sunnah.
التفسير النبوي: آيات بيّنها النبي ﷺ: The Prophetic exegesis: verses the Prophet ﷺ explained
آيات فسّرها النبي ﷺ بنفسه أو بيّن المراد: Verses that the Prophet ﷺ himself interpreted or clarified when asked, which is the soundest exegesis and the most worthy of acceptance. Each item gives the verse, the wording of the hadith with its source, how the two connect and a quotation from an exegete.
آيات تلاها النبي ﷺ أو قال فيها «اقرؤوا إ: Verses the Prophet ﷺ recited, or about which he said "Recite if you wish"
أحاديث استشهد فيها النبي ﷺ أو راويه بآية: Hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ, or the narrator, cites a verse, saying "Recite if you wish" or "then he recited", so that the verse confirms what he reported about the Hereafter, character or rulings.
فضل آيات وسور بعينها: The merit of specific verses and surahs
أحاديث صحيحة سمّت آيات وسوراً من القرآن: Sound hadith that name particular verses and surahs and state their merit, given here with their wording and the verse itself. Details of ruqya and daily remembrance are in their own sections, "Healing with the Quran" and "Morning and evening adhkar".
أحاديث ذكرت نزول آيات: Hadith that mention the revelation of verses
أحاديث صحيحة صرّح فيها الراوي بأن آية نز: Sound hadith in which the narrator states that a verse was revealed about a particular event or that the Prophet ﷺ spoke at its revelation. The science of the occasions of revelation is covered in the "Sciences of the Quran" section; here is what is sound in the hadith, in its own words.
آيات عمل بها النبي ﷺ في دعائه وذكره: Verses the Prophet ﷺ acted on in his supplication and remembrance
أحاديث ذكر فيها دعاء النبي ﷺ أو عمله بمق: Hadith that mention the Prophet's supplication or action in accordance with a verse, so the verse is turned into practice.
طاعة الله والرسول ﷺ: Obeying Allah and the Messenger ﷺ
قرن الله طاعة الرسول ﷺ بطاعته في الآية،: The verse joins obedience to the Messenger ﷺ with obedience to Allah, and the hadith explains that obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah and disobeying him is disobeying Allah.
من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah
الآية تقرر أن طاعة الرسول ﷺ طاعة لله، وا: The verse establishes that obeying the Messenger ﷺ is obeying Allah, and the hadith makes obeying him the way into Paradise and disobeying him a refusal of it.
وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه: What the Messenger gives you, take
استدل ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه بالآية على: Ibn Mas'ud cited the verse to show that what the Messenger ﷺ forbade is forbidden in the Book of Allah, since the verse commands taking what he brought.
لتبيّن للناس ما نُزّل إليهم: That you may make clear to people what was sent down to them
بيّن الله أن مهمة الرسول ﷺ شرح ما نزل إل: Allah made explaining what was revealed part of the Messenger's mission, and the hadith warns that the Sunnah is revelation to be acted on like the Quran, so one may not suffice with the Quran alone.
لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة: You have in the Messenger of Allah a good example
أمر الله بالتأسي بالنبي ﷺ، وفي الحديثين: Allah commands following the Prophet ﷺ as a model, and the two hadith apply this: acts of worship are performed as people saw him perform them, in prayer and in Hajj.
فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكّموك: No, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you the judge
روى الزبير أن الآية نزلت في خصومته مع رج: Al-Zubayr reported that the verse was revealed about his dispute with a man of the Ansar which the Prophet ﷺ judged; it shows that faith is not complete without submission to his judgment, outwardly and inwardly.
إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني: If you love Allah, then follow me
جعلت الآية اتباع النبي ﷺ علامة محبة الله: The verse makes following the Prophet ﷺ the sign of loving Allah, and the hadith sets the measure for accepting deeds: that they accord with his command.
فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره: Let those who oppose his command beware
حذّرت الآية من مخالفة أمره ﷺ، وجاء الحدي: The verse warns against opposing his command, and the hadith concerns whoever turns away from his Sunnah even with the intention of worship, showing that following him is required.
وما ينطق عن الهوى: He does not speak from desire
قرّرت الآية أن ما ينطق به النبي ﷺ وحي، و: The verse establishes that what the Prophet ﷺ speaks is revelation, and the hadith confirms that nothing comes from him but the truth, so no part of his established Sunnah is to be rejected.
الظلم المراد بالآية: الشرك: The "wrongdoing" in the verse is shirk
شقّ على الصحابة أن يُحمل «الظلم» على كل: It troubled the Companions to take "wrongdoing" as every sin, so the Prophet ﷺ explained that here it means shirk and cited the verse of Luqman.
سمّى النبي ﷺ يوم الأحزاب الصلاة الوسطى ب: On the day of al-Ahzab the Prophet ﷺ named the middle prayer as the Asr prayer, which became among the strongest evidence cited in explaining the verse.
فسّر النبي ﷺ «القوة» في الآية بالرمي وكر: The Prophet ﷺ explained "power" in the verse as archery and repeated it three times for emphasis, interpreting the general term by its greatest instance.
الزيادة: النظر إلى وجه الله: The "increase": looking at the Face of Allah
ثبت في الحديث أن «الزيادة» في الآية هي ا: The hadith establishes that the "increase" in the verse is looking at the noble Face of Allah, the greatest delight of the people of Paradise; in a narration of Muslim the Prophet ﷺ then recited: "For those who did good is the best and an increase."
سألت عائشة رضي الله عنها عن «الحساب اليس: Aisha asked about the "easy reckoning", and the Prophet ﷺ explained that it is the mere presentation before Allah; whoever has his reckoning examined in detail is ruined.
الأمة الوسط شهداء على الناس: A middle nation, witnesses over mankind
فسّر النبي ﷺ الشهادة في الآية بشهادة هذه: The Prophet ﷺ explained the witnessing in the verse as this community's testimony for Nuh and the prophets that they conveyed the message, and stated that "middle" means just.
جعل النبي ﷺ الدعاء هو العبادة وقرأ الآية: The Prophet ﷺ made supplication the very worship and recited the verse, which shows that abandoning supplication is arrogance toward worship and that supplication is the root of worship.
القول الثابت عند السؤال في القبر: The firm word when questioned in the grave
بيّن النبي ﷺ أن «القول الثابت» هو جواب ا: The Prophet ﷺ explained that the "firm word" is the believer's answer in the grave by the two testimonies.
الكلمة الطيبة كشجرة طيبة: النخلة: The good word like a good tree: the date palm
ضرب النبي ﷺ المثل بشجرة لا يسقط ورقها وب: The Prophet ﷺ gave the parable of a tree whose leaves never fall and said it is like the Muslim, which clarifies the "good tree" of the verse as the date palm.
ختم قتادة حديث الشفاعة الطويل بأن النبي: Qatada ends the long hadith of intercession by relating that the Prophet ﷺ recited the verse and said this is the Praised Station that Allah promised His Prophet, the station of intercession.
فسّر النبي ﷺ الكوثر في ليلة المعراج بأنه: On the night of the Ascension the Prophet ﷺ explained al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise whose banks have domes of hollow pearl.
المحكم والمتشابه: من يتبع المتشابه: The clear and the ambiguous: those who follow the ambiguous
تلا النبي ﷺ الآية وبيّن أن من يتتبع المت: The Prophet ﷺ recited the verse and explained that those who pursue the ambiguous are the ones Allah named, and ordered caution against them.
من رآه النبي ﷺ عند سدرة المنتهى: Whom the Prophet saw at the Lote Tree
سألت عائشة رضي الله عنها النبي ﷺ عن قوله: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ about "and he certainly saw him in another descent", and he explained that the one seen was Jibril, peace be upon him, in his true form.
يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين: The day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds
وصف النبي ﷺ هول الوقوف يوم القيامة بأن ا: The Prophet ﷺ described the terror of the standing on the Day of Resurrection: sweat reaches people up to the middle of their ears.
بيّن النبي ﷺ أن الفاتحة هي «السبع المثان: The Prophet ﷺ explained that al-Fatiha is the "seven oft-repeated verses and the great Quran" of the verse, and the greatest surah in the Quran.
ما أخفي للصالحين: What is hidden for the righteous
أخبر النبي ﷺ عن الله أنه أعدّ للصالحين م: The Prophet ﷺ reported from Allah that He has prepared for the righteous what no heart has conceived, then referred to the verse that confirms it.
استدل النبي ﷺ بالآية على عظم شجر الجنة،: The Prophet ﷺ cited the verse to show the greatness of the trees of Paradise: a rider travels a hundred years in the shade of one tree.
أخبر النبي ﷺ أن الرحم تعلّقت بالرحمن تست: The Prophet ﷺ reported that the womb clung to the Merciful seeking refuge from being severed, and Abu Hurayra recited the verse that warns against cutting it.
النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم: The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves
قال النبي ﷺ إنه أولى بكل مؤمن في الدنيا: The Prophet ﷺ said he is closest to every believer in this world and the next and recited the verse, then stated the ruling for one who dies leaving debt or wealth.
أخبر النبي ﷺ أن الله يمهل الظالم حتى إذا: The Prophet ﷺ reported that Allah gives the wrongdoer respite until, when He seizes him, he is not let go, and he recited the verse as evidence.
خطب النبي ﷺ فأخبر بحال الحشر، وتلا الآية: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon describing the state of the gathering and recited the verse as confirmation that the return is like the beginning, a promise from Allah.
فاتحة الكتاب وخواتيم البقرة نوران: Al-Fatiha and the end of al-Baqara are two lights
بشّر مَلَك النبيَّ ﷺ بنورين لم يُؤتهما ن: An angel gave the Prophet ﷺ glad tidings of two lights given to no prophet before him: al-Fatiha and the closing verses of al-Baqara.
علّم الشيطان أبا هريرة وهو سارق أن قراءة: The devil taught Abu Hurayra, as he was stealing, that reciting Ayat al-Kursi at bedtime protects, and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it, saying: he told you the truth though he is a liar.
الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة: The last two verses of al-Baqara
ورد أن من قرأ الآيتين الأخيرتين من البقر: It is reported that whoever recites the last two verses of al-Baqara in a night, they suffice him; scholars of the hadith recorded several views on the meaning of "suffice him".
سمع رجل رجلاً يردد «قل هو الله أحد» فاست: A man heard another repeating "Say: He is Allah, One" and thought little of it, so the Prophet ﷺ told him it equals a third of the Quran because of the monotheism it contains.
أخبر النبي ﷺ عقبة بن عامر بأن آيات أُنزل: The Prophet ﷺ told Uqba ibn Amir that verses had been revealed that night the like of which had never been seen: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak" and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind".
عشر آيات من أول الكهف: The first ten verses of al-Kahf
ورد أن من حفظ عشر آيات من أول الكهف عُصم: It is reported that whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal.
سورة الملك ثلاثون آية، وقد ورد أنها تشفع: Surat al-Mulk has thirty verses and it is reported that it intercedes for its reciter until he is forgiven; the hadith is in the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi, with the grade shown below.
سورة البقرة وطرد الشيطان: Surat al-Baqara drives away the devil
أمر النبي ﷺ بقراءة القرآن في البيوت وأخب: The Prophet ﷺ commanded reciting the Quran in homes and reported that the devil flees from a house in which Surat al-Baqara is recited.
أخبر النبي ﷺ أنه أُنزلت عليه سورة هي أحب: The Prophet ﷺ said a surah had been revealed to him that was dearer to him than the world and all it contains, then recited "Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest".
لما نزلت الآية صعد النبي ﷺ الصفا فنادى ق: When the verse was revealed the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Safa, called Quraysh and warned them; Abu Lahab objected and "May the hands of Abu Lahab perish" was revealed.
النهي عن الاستغفار للمشركين: The prohibition of seeking forgiveness for polytheists
قال النبي ﷺ لعمه عند موته إنه سيستغفر له: The Prophet ﷺ told his uncle at his death that he would seek forgiveness for him unless forbidden, and the prohibition of seeking forgiveness for polytheists was revealed.
إنك لا تهدي من أحببت: You do not guide whom you love
عرض النبي ﷺ الشهادة على عمه أبي طالب عند: The Prophet ﷺ offered the testimony of faith to his uncle Abu Talib at his death and he refused, so Allah revealed that guidance is in His hand alone.
اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم: This day I have perfected your religion
سأل يهودي عمرَ عن آية في القرآن لو نزلت: A Jew asked Umar about a verse that, had it been revealed to them, they would have taken its day as a feast; Umar explained that it was revealed at Arafa on a Friday.
إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله: Al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the signs of Allah
بيّنت رواية الباب أن الآية نزلت لرفع الح: The narration shows that the verse was revealed to remove the hesitation some of the Ansar and others felt about walking between al-Safa and al-Marwa.
الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود: The white thread from the black thread
فهم عدي بن حاتم الآية على ظاهرها فبيّن ل: Adi ibn Hatim understood the verse literally, so the Prophet ﷺ explained that what is meant is the darkness of night and the whiteness of day.
قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذاباً: Say: He is able to send punishment upon you
استعاذ النبي ﷺ بوجه الله عند نزول أوائل: The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge in the Face of Allah as the first parts of the verse were revealed, and when "or confuse you into factions" was revealed he said: "These two are lighter or easier."
كان أكثر دعاء النبي ﷺ دعاء الآية، وهو جا: The supplication of the verse was the Prophet's most frequent, a comprehensive request for the good of this world and the Hereafter.
الآيات العشر من آل عمران عند القيام بالل: The verses of Al Imran at night prayer
كان النبي ﷺ إذا قام في الثلث الأخير من ا: In the last third of the night the Prophet ﷺ would look to the sky and recite the verse, then perform ablution and pray.
قول إبراهيم وعيسى: اللهم أمتي: The words of Ibrahim and Isa: "My community, my community"
تلا النبي ﷺ قول إبراهيم وعيسى عليهما الس: The Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Ibrahim and Isa, peace be upon them, raised his hands and wept praying for his community, and Allah gave him glad tidings that He would please him regarding them.
سورة النصر والتسبيح بحمد الله: Surat al-Nasr and glorifying with praise
بيّنت عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي ﷺ كان: Aisha explained that the Prophet ﷺ acted on "glorify with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness" and said the glorification and the request for forgiveness frequently.
أحاديث صحيحة بنصها وتخريجها مرتبطة بآيات: Sound hadith with their texts and sources linked to their verses: the Sunnah in the Quran, Prophetic exegesis, verses the Prophet ﷺ recited, the merit of verses and surahs and the revelation of verses, with the exegetes' words.
وللأحاديث الجامعة انظر «الأحاديث الأربع: For the comprehensive hadith, see "The Forty Hadith of al-Nawawi".
الوصايا والأوامر والتوجيهات المباشرة الت: The direct commands, prohibitions and counsels with which Allah addressed His servants in the Quran, arranged by subject: each counsel with its verses in the Mushaf script and a verbatim quotation from the books of exegesis.
هذا الركن للتوصية الصريحة نفسها: ما أمر: This section is about the explicit counsel itself: what Allah commanded His servants, forbade them or enjoined upon them in the verses. It therefore does not repeat "The Function of Man in the Quran" (the purpose and mission of creation), "Categories of People" (the kinds of those addressed), or "Fiqh of Worship" and "Fiqh from the Noble Quran" (the detail of rulings). The titles and summaries are our concise wording of what the verses themselves indicate; the verses and the exegetes' quotations are given in their own words from the bundled sources.
نصوص الآيات بلفظ مصحف المدينة النبوية (م: Verses are in the wording of the Madinah Mushaf (King Fahd Complex, version 18) and its script; the quotations are from Tafsir al-Sa'di in its own words from the bundled book, with bracketed words as in the original book, and a trailing ellipsis marks an excerpt cut from the sentence. Nothing is attributed to Allah in this section except what the verses state.
توصيات القرآن الكريم من كلام رب العالمين: The Quran's Counsels in the Words of the Lord of the Worlds
مواضع جمعت فيها الآيات أصول الوصايا في م: Passages in which the verses gather the foundations of the divine counsel in one place, among them the ten counsels in Surat al-An'am, which end with the words "That is what He has enjoined upon you".
وصية لقمان لابنه: The Counsel of Luqman to His Son
ما حكاه القرآن من وعظ لقمان الحكيم لابنه: What the Quran relates of the admonition of Luqman the Wise to his son, in the midst of which comes the counsel of Allah concerning parents.
توصيات ربانية في التقوى والعبادة وإقامة: Divine counsels on piety, worship, upholding the religion, prayer, remembrance, gratitude and patience.
توصيات في برّ الوالدين ورعاية الأولاد وح: Counsels on dutifulness to parents, caring for children, kind companionship and protecting one's family.
توصيات في القول السديد والعفو والتثبّت و: Counsels on upright speech, forgiveness, verifying reports, guarding honour, seeking permission and lowering the gaze.
توصيات في أكل المال بالحق وتوثيق الديون: Counsels on earning lawfully, documenting debts, leaving usury, fulfilling contracts, spending, the orphan's property and bequests.
في المجتمع والعدل والدعوة: On Society, Justice and Calling to Allah
توصيات في أداء الأمانات والقيام بالقسط و: Counsels on returning trusts, upholding justice, cooperating in righteousness, reconciling people, calling with wisdom and obeying those in authority in what is right.
التواصي بالحق والصبر والمرحمة: Counselling One Another to Truth, Patience and Mercy
آيات جعلت التواصي نفسه خُلُقاً للمؤمنين:: Verses that make mutual counselling itself a trait of the believers: urging one another to truth, patience and mercy.
الوصايا العشر: الأولى إلى الخامسة: The Ten Counsels: the First Five
خمس وصايا: تحريم الشرك بالله، ثم الإحسان: Five counsels: forbidding shirk, then kindness to parents, not killing children out of poverty, avoiding indecencies open and hidden, and not taking the life Allah has made sacred except by right, and end with "That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may use reason".
الوصايا العشر: السادسة إلى التاسعة: The Ten Counsels: the Sixth to the Ninth
أربع وصايا: ألا يُقرب مال اليتيم إلا بال: Four counsels: do not approach the orphan's property except in the best way, give full measure and weight with justice, speak justly even about a relative, and fulfil the covenant of Allah; it ends with "That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may remember".
الوصايا العشر: العاشرة والصراط المستقيم: The Ten Counsels: the Tenth and the Straight Path
والوصية العاشرة: هذا صراط الله مستقيماً: The tenth counsel: this is Allah's straight path, so follow it and do not follow the divergent paths that scatter you from His way; it ends with "That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous".
عبادة الله وحده وبرّ الوالدين: Worshipping Allah Alone and Honouring Parents
قضاء الله أن لا يُعبد إلا هو، وأن يُحسَن: Allah decreed that none be worshipped but Him and that parents be treated with kindness; at their old age one must not say "uff" to them but speak a generous word and lower the wing of humility out of mercy.
حقّ القربى والمسكين والاعتدال في الإنفاق: The Right of Relatives and the Needy, and Moderation in Spending
إيتاء ذي القربى والمسكين وابن السبيل حقّ: Give relatives, the needy and the wayfarer their due, do not squander, and neither tie your hand to your neck nor open it completely.
حفظ الأنفس والأعراض والأموال والعهود: Protecting Lives, Honour, Property and Covenants
النهي عن قتل الأولاد خشية الفقر، وعن قرب: Do not kill your children out of fear of poverty, do not approach adultery, do not take the life Allah has made sacred except by right, do not approach the orphan's property except in the best way, fulfil covenants and give full measure and weight with a true balance.
التثبّت من العلم والتواضع في المشي: Verifying Knowledge and Humility in Walking
لا يتبع الإنسان ما ليس له به علم، فالسمع: Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of, for hearing, sight and heart will all be questioned; and do not walk upon the earth exultantly, for you will never tear the earth apart nor reach the mountains in height.
الإحسان إلى كل ذي حق: Kindness to Everyone with a Right
عبادة الله وحده بلا شرك، والإحسان إلى ال: Worship Allah alone, do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbour near and far, the companion at one's side, the wayfarer and those under one's authority; Allah does not love the arrogant and boastful.
العدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى: Justice, Excellence and Giving to Relatives
أمر الله بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القرب: Allah commands justice, excellence and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing and oppression; He admonishes so that people may remember.
ليس البرّ توجيه الوجوه قبل المشرق والمغر: Righteousness is not turning your faces toward east or west, but belief in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book and the prophets, giving wealth despite loving it, establishing prayer, paying zakah, keeping covenants and patience in hardship and in battle.
أول وصية: الأمر بشكر الله، وأول ما وعظ ب: The first counsel is to thank Allah; the first thing Luqman admonished his son with was "Do not associate anything with Allah; indeed shirk is a great injustice".
وصّى الله الإنسان بوالديه، وذكر حمل الأم: Allah enjoined man to honour his parents, recalling the mother's hardship in bearing him and his weaning in two years; to thank Him and them, and to accompany them kindly in this world even if they strive to make him commit shirk, without obeying them in it.
مراقبة الله في الصغير والكبير: Being Mindful of Allah in the Small and the Great
ولو كان العمل مثقال حبة من خردل في صخرة: Even if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed hidden in a rock or in the heavens or the earth, Allah will bring it forth; Allah is Subtle and All-Aware.
إقامة الصلاة، والأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن: Establish prayer, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you; that is among the matters requiring resolve.
النهي عن تصعير الخد للناس وعن المشي في ا: Do not turn your cheek away from people in pride nor walk the earth exultantly; be moderate in your pace and lower your voice.
وصية الله للأولين والآخرين: اتقوا الله: Allah's Counsel to the First and the Last: Fear Allah
نصّت الآية أن الله وصّى الذين أوتوا الكت: The verse states that Allah enjoined those given the Book before us, and us, to fear Allah, and that to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth, and He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
نداء لجميع الناس أن يعبدوا ربهم الذي خلق: A call to all people to worship their Lord who created them and those before them so that they may become righteous, who made the earth a bed and the sky a canopy, so they should set up no equals to Him.
أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه: Establish the Religion and Do Not Divide in It
شرع الله لنا من الدين ما وصّى به نوحاً و: Allah has ordained for us of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, what He revealed to Muhammad, and what He enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa and Isa: establish the religion and do not be divided in it.
الأمر بالمحافظة على الصلوات والصلاة الوس: Guard the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly; and when safe, remember Allah as He taught what we did not know.
نداء للمؤمنين أن يذكروا الله ذكراً كثيرا: A call to the believers to remember Allah much and to glorify Him morning and evening.
Remember Me and I will remember you; be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابط: O you who believe, be patient, persevere, stay vigilant and fear Allah so that you may succeed.
اتقوا الله حق تقاته واعتصموا بحبله: Fear Allah as He Should Be Feared and Hold Fast to His Rope
الأمر بتقوى الله حق تقاته وأن لا نموت إل: Fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims; hold fast together to the rope of Allah and do not divide; remember Allah's favour in joining your hearts.
افتتح الله آية المواريث بقوله «يوصيكم ال: Allah opens the verse of inheritance with "Allah instructs you concerning your children", then states the shares of children and parents, after any bequest or debt, as an obligation from Him.
وصية الله بالوالدين وشكر النعمة: Allah's Counsel About Parents and Thanking His Favour
وصّى الله الإنسان بوالديه إحساناً، وذكر: Allah enjoined man to treat his parents with kindness, recalling how his mother bore and delivered him with hardship, and that bearing and weaning take thirty months; and the supplication of one reaching forty years to be inspired to thank Allah's favour and to have righteous offspring.
برّ الوالدين وحدّه عند الشرك: Kindness to Parents and Its Limit at Shirk
وصّى الله الإنسان بوالديه حسناً، فإن جاه: Allah enjoined man to treat his parents with goodness, but if they strive to make him associate with Allah what he has no knowledge of, he should not obey them; to Allah is the return of all.
وصية إبراهيم ويعقوب لبنيهما: The Counsel of Ibrahim and Yaqub to Their Sons
وصّى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب: «يا بنيّ إ: Ibrahim enjoined it upon his sons, and Yaqub also: "My sons, Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims"; and Yaqub asked his sons at his death what they would worship after him.
أمر الله نبيه أن يأمر أهله بالصلاة ويصطب: Allah commanded His Prophet to order his family to pray and to be steadfast in it, and told him that He does not ask him for provision but provides for him, and that the outcome is for righteousness.
قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم ناراً: Protect Yourselves and Your Families from a Fire
خطاب للمؤمنين أن يقوا أنفسهم وأهليهم نار: A call to the believers to protect themselves and their families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are stern and severe angels who do not disobey Allah in what He commands.
نهي عن إرث النساء كرهاً وعن عضلهن، وأمر: Do not inherit women against their will nor constrain them, and live with them in kindness; if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.
اتقوا الله وقولوا قولاً سديداً: Fear Allah and Speak Upright Words
تقوى الله والقول السديد سبب لإصلاح الأعم: Fearing Allah and upright speech lead to the amendment of deeds and forgiveness of sins; whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has achieved a great success.
من ميثاق بني إسرائيل: عبادة الله وحده، و: Part of the covenant with the Children of Israel: worship Allah alone, be good to parents, relatives, orphans and the needy, speak good words to people, establish prayer and give zakah.
خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين: Accept Forgiveness, Enjoin What Is Right and Turn Away from the Ignorant
جمعت الآية حسن الخلق: أخذ العفو وما تيسّ: The verse gathers good character: accept what people readily give, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
لا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة، فيُؤمر بدفع: The good deed and the evil deed are not equal; repel evil with what is better, and the one between whom and you was enmity becomes as though he were a close friend; none is granted it except those who are patient and those of great fortune.
التثبّت من خبر الفاسق: Verifying the Report of a Wrongdoer
إن جاء فاسق بنبأ فتبيّنوا لئلا تصيبوا قو: If a wrongdoer brings you news, verify it, lest you harm people out of ignorance and become regretful for what you have done.
النهي عن سخرية قوم من قوم وعن اللمز والت: Do not let a people mock another people, do not defame one another or call each other by offensive names, and avoid much suspicion, spying and backbiting.
غضّ البصر وحفظ الفروج: Lowering the Gaze and Guarding Chastity
أمر الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات أن يغضوا من: Allah commanded believing men and women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, which is purer for them; Allah is aware of what they do.
لا تدخلوا بيوتاً غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا: Do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked leave and greeted their people, and if you are told to go back, then go back; that is purer for you.
لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل: Do Not Consume Each Other's Wealth Unjustly
نهي عن أكل الأموال بالباطل واستثناء التج: Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except through trade by mutual consent, and do not kill yourselves; Allah is Merciful to you.
اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا: Fear Allah and Give Up What Remains of Usury
أمر الله المؤمنين أن يتقوه ويذروا ما بقي: Allah commanded the believers to fear Him and give up what remains of usury; those who do not are warned of war from Allah and His Messenger; they keep their capital, and the one in difficulty is to be given time.
أمر الله إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى ب: When you contract a debt for a set term, Allah commands that it be written down justly, that the scribe not refuse, that the debtor dictate and fear Allah without diminishing anything, and that witnesses be called.
يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود، وهي أ: O you who believe, fulfil your contracts; the command to keep faith with every commitment the believer makes with his Lord and with people.
أمر بالإنفاق من طيب الكسب وما أخرج الله: Spend from the good that you have earned and what We have brought out of the earth for you; do not choose the worthless to spend; beware of the Devil's threat of poverty, while Allah promises forgiveness and bounty.
كتب الله على من حضره الموت وترك خيراً أن: Allah prescribed for one who is about to die and leaves wealth to bequeath to parents and relatives in fairness, a duty upon the righteous, and warned whoever alters the bequest after hearing it.
وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث: Give orphans their property and do not substitute the bad for the good nor consume their property with your own; that is a great sin.
أداء الأمانات والحكم بالعدل: Returning Trusts and Judging with Justice
يأمر الله أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها، و: Allah commands that trusts be returned to their owners, and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; excellent is what He admonishes you with.
كونوا قوّامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أ: Be persistently standing firm for justice, as witnesses for Allah, even against yourselves, parents and relatives, and do not follow desire so as not to be just.
العدل ولو مع من نبغض: Justice Even Toward Those We Dislike
لا يحملنّكم بغض قوم على ألا تعدلوا، اعدل: Do not let hatred for a people lead you to injustice; be just, for that is nearer to righteousness.
وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا عل: Cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression.
أمة تدعو إلى الخير: A Community Calling to What Is Good
ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون ب: Let there be among you a community calling to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong; they are the successful.
ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة: Call to the Way of Your Lord with Wisdom
ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة: Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner.
إن اقتتلت طائفتان من المؤمنين فأصلحوا بي: If two groups of believers fight, reconcile between them; if one oppresses the other, fight the oppressor until it returns to Allah's command, and act justly; the believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers.
طاعة الله والرسول وأولي الأمر بالمعروف: Obeying Allah, the Messenger and Those in Authority in What Is Right
أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر م: Obey Allah, obey the Messenger and those in authority among you, and if you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger if you believe in Allah and the Last Day.
التواصي بالحق والصبر: Counselling One Another to Truth and Patience
الإنسان في خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا ال: Mankind is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds and counsel one another to truth and to patience.
التواصي بالصبر وبالمرحمة: Counselling One Another to Patience and to Mercy
فسّر الله العقبة: فكّ رقبة أو إطعام في ي: Allah explained the steep path: freeing a slave or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan or a needy person, then being among those who believe and counsel one another to patience and to compassion.
{ذلكم}: المذكور، {وصَّاكم}[الله]{به لعلّ: "That" which is mentioned, "He has enjoined upon you that you may use reason": that you understand His counsel from Allah, then preserve it, then observe it and act on it. The verse shows that a person's fulfilment of what Allah commands is in proportion to his reason.
{وبعهد الله أوفوا}: وهذا يشملُ العهد الذ: "And fulfil the covenant of Allah": this includes the covenant made with Allah by servants, to uphold His rights and fulfil them, and the covenants made between people; all of it must be fulfilled and breaking or neglecting it is forbidden. "That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may remember": what He has explained to you of the rulings, so that you uphold Allah's counsel as it should be upheld and understand the wisdom and rulings in it.
ولما بيَّن كثيراً من الأوامر الكبار والش: When He had explained many of the great commands and important laws, He pointed to them and to what is more general, saying "And that this is My path, straight": these rulings and what resembles them, which Allah explained in His Book and made clear to His servants, are Allah's path leading to Him and to the abode of His honour, balanced, easy and direct. "So follow it": so that you attain success and fulfil your hopes; "and do not follow the other ways", those opposing this way, "for they will separate you from His way", leading you astray right and left; and if you stray from the straight path there remain only roads that lead to Hell. "That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous": for if you uphold what Allah has made clear to you in knowledge and action, you become of the righteous and successful servants of Allah.
ثم ذكر بعد حقِّه القيام بحقِّ الوالدين،: Then, after His own right, He mentioned fulfilling the right of parents, saying "and to parents, kindness": be good to them in every way, in word and deed, for they are the cause of a person's existence and have such love for the child, kindness toward him and closeness as make the right firm and dutifulness obligatory. "If one or both of them reach old age with you", an age at which their strength weakens and they need the kindness and gentleness that is customary, "do not say to them 'uff'": the least degree of harm, mentioned to alert to all that exceeds it, meaning do not harm them in the slightest; "and do not repel them", that is, scold them or speak harshly to them. "And speak to them a generous word": in words they love, with courtesy and gentle, good speech that delights their hearts and calms their souls, which varies with circumstances, customs and times.
يقول تعالى: {وآت ذا القُربى حقَّه}: من ا: Allah the Exalted says: "And give the relative his right", of kindness and honour, obligatory and recommended, a right that varies with conditions, kin, need or lack of it, and times; "and the needy": give him his right of zakah and otherwise so that his neediness is removed; "and the wayfarer": the stranger cut off from his land. All are given of the wealth in a way that does not harm the giver and does not exceed the fitting measure, for that is squandering which Allah has forbidden, and He declared that the squanderers "are brothers of the devils" …
وهذا من رحمته بعباده؛ حيث كان أرحم بهم م: This is from His mercy toward His servants, for He is more merciful to them than their own parents: He forbade parents to kill their children for fear of poverty, took responsibility for providing for all, and declared that "killing them is ever a great sin", that is, one of the gravest major sins, for it removes mercy from the heart, is the worst disobedience of duty, and shows audacity in killing children who have committed no wrong or sin.
أي: ولا تتَّبع ما ليس لك به علم، بل تثبّ: That is: do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; rather, verify everything you say and do, and do not think it will pass without consequence for or against you. "Indeed the hearing, the sight and the heart, all of those will be questioned": so it is fitting for a servant who knows he is accountable for what he said and did, and for how he used the faculties Allah created for His worship, to prepare an answer for the questioning, which happens only by using them in the service of Allah, devoting religion sincerely to Him and restraining them from what Allah dislikes.
يأمر تعالى عباده بعبادتِهِ وحدَه لا شريك: Allah the Exalted commands His servants to worship Him alone with no partner, which is to enter under the yoke of His servitude and submit to His commands and prohibitions with love, humility and sincerity in all outward and inward acts of worship, and He forbids associating anything with Him, neither minor nor major …
فصارت هذه الآية جامعةً لجميع المأمورات و: So this verse became comprehensive of all commands and prohibitions; nothing is left that does not fall under it. It is a rule to which all particulars return: every matter that contains justice, excellence or giving to relatives is among what Allah commanded, and every matter that contains indecency, wrongdoing or oppression is among what He forbade; by it the goodness of what Allah commanded and the ugliness of what He forbade become known, and people's sayings are measured by it and all conditions are referred to it. Blessed is He who placed in His speech guidance, healing, light and the criterion between all things; hence He says "He admonishes you", by what He has made clear in His Book, commanding you what is most beneficial and forbidding you what harms you.
{أولئك}؛ أي: المتصفون بما ذكر من العقائد: "Those": those described with the good beliefs and deeds that are the traces, proof and light of faith, and the character that is the beauty and reality of humanity, are "the ones who have been true" in their faith because their deeds proved their faith, "and it is they who are the righteous", because they left what is forbidden and did what is commanded. These matters contain all virtues, by implication and necessity, because fulfilling covenants includes the whole religion, and because the acts of worship named in this verse are the greatest; whoever upholds them is more upright in everything else. They are the righteous, truthful, God-fearing.
{وإذ قال لقمانُ لابنِهِ وهو يَعِظُهُ}؛ أ: "And when Luqman said to his son while he was admonishing him": admonition is command and prohibition joined with encouragement and warning; he commanded him to be sincere and forbade shirk and gave him the reason: "Indeed, shirk is a great injustice". Its greatness lies in nothing being more terrible than equating a creature made from dust with the Lord of all necks, equating one who owns nothing of the matter with the Owner of the whole matter, equating the deficient and needy in every respect with the perfect, self-sufficient Lord, and equating one who never gave the weight of an atom of favour with Him from whom comes every favour in people's religion, worldly life, hereafter, hearts and bodies, and who alone averts harm. Is there any injustice greater than this?
ولما أمر بالقيام بحقِّه بترك الشرك الذي: After commanding the upholding of His right by abandoning shirk, which necessitates upholding tawhid, He commanded upholding the right of parents, saying "And We have enjoined upon man": We entrusted him and made it a charge with him for which We will question him whether he kept it or not. We enjoined him "concerning his parents" and said to him "Be grateful to Me": by upholding My servitude, fulfilling My rights and not using My favours to disobey Me; "and to your parents": by kindness to them in gentle speech, courteous words and good deeds, humility toward them, honouring and revering them, bearing their expenses and avoiding harming them in every way in word and deed. We enjoined him with this counsel and informed him that "to Me is the final destination": you will return, O man, to the One who enjoined and charged you with these rights, and He will ask whether you fulfilled them and reward you abundantly, or neglected them and punish you severely.
{يا بنيَّ إنَّها إن تَكُ مثقالَ حبةٍ من: "O my son, indeed if it should be the weight of a mustard seed", the smallest and most insignificant of things, "and should be within a rock", in its middle, "or in the heavens or in the earth", in whichever direction of them, "Allah will bring it forth", by the vastness of His knowledge, completeness of His awareness and perfection of His power; so He said "Indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware", subtle in His knowledge and awareness until He knows the inner depths, secrets and hidden corners of wastelands and seas. The aim is to urge mindfulness of Allah and obedience to Him as far as possible, and to warn against doing wrong, small or great.
{يا بنيَّ أقِمِ الصَّلاة}: حثَّه عليها و: "O my son, establish prayer": he urged him to it and singled it out because it is the greatest bodily act of worship; "and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong": that requires knowing what is right in order to enjoin it and what is wrong in order to forbid it, and requires what enjoining and forbidding cannot be complete without, such as gentleness and patience, as he made explicit in "and be patient over what befalls you", and also being one who does what he enjoins and refrains from what he forbids. This includes perfecting himself by doing good and leaving evil, and perfecting others by his enjoining and forbidding. Since it is known that one who enjoins and forbids will inevitably be tried, and that enjoining and forbidding is burdensome to souls, he commanded him to be patient, saying "Indeed, that which Luqman admonished his son with is of the matters requiring resolve": matters one resolves upon and cares about, which only people of resolve are granted.
{ولا تُصَعِّرۡ خدَّك للناس}؛ أي: لا تُمِ: "And do not turn your cheek away from people", that is, do not tilt it and frown at people in arrogance and self-importance, "and do not walk upon the earth exultantly", that is, in pride and boasting over favours, forgetting the Giver of favours and admiring yourself. "Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded", in himself, appearance and self-importance, "and boastful": in his speech.
يخبر تعالى عن عموم ملكه العظيم الواسع ال: He informs of the vastness of His great and wide dominion, which necessitates His managing it with every kind of management and disposing it with every kind of disposal, in decree and in law; His legislative disposal is that He enjoined the first and the last, the people of earlier and later books, with piety, which includes command, prohibition, legislating rulings and recompensing those who uphold this counsel with reward and those who neglect and lose it with painful punishment …
هذا أمر عام لجميع الناس بأمر عام وهو الع: This is a general command to all people to a general act, namely the comprehensive worship that includes obeying Allah's commands, avoiding His prohibitions and believing His reports. He commanded them to do what He created them for; the Exalted said "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me". Then He gave proof for the obligation of worshipping Him alone: that He is your Lord who nurtured you with all kinds of favours, created you after non-existence, and created those before you.
ولهذا قال:{أنۡ أقيموا الدِّين}؛ أي: أمرك: Hence He said "that you establish the religion": He commanded you to establish all the laws of the religion, its fundamentals and branches, establishing it yourselves, striving to establish it among others, cooperating in righteousness and piety and not cooperating in sin and aggression; "and do not be divided therein": so that you agree on the fundamentals and branches of the religion, and take care that issues do not divide you and split you into factions, becoming sects that oppose one another although you agree on the root of your religion. Among the forms of unity upon the religion and not dividing in it is what the Lawgiver commanded of general gatherings, such as the gathering of Hajj, the festivals, Fridays, the five prayers and jihad, and other acts of worship that are neither complete nor perfect except by gathering for them and not dividing.
يأمر تعالى بالمحافظة {على الصلوات}؛ عموم: The Exalted commands guarding "the prayers" in general and "the middle prayer", which is the afternoon prayer, in particular; guarding them means performing them at their time, with their conditions, pillars, humility and everything obligatory and recommended in them. By guarding the prayers, guarding all other acts of worship is achieved, and prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing, especially when one perfects it as commanded by His words "and stand before Allah devoutly", meaning humble, sincere and submissive, for devoutness is continuous obedience with humility.
يأمر تعالى المؤمنين بذكره ذكراً كثيراً؛: The Exalted commands the believers to remember Him much, by tahlil, tahmid, tasbih, takbir and every statement that brings nearness to Allah; the least of that is for a person to keep to the morning and evening adhkar, those after the five prayers and at occasions and causes, and it is fitting to persist in it at all times and in all conditions, for it is an act of worship in which the doer gets ahead while resting, a call to the love and knowledge of Allah, a help to good, and a restraint of the tongue from foul speech.
{فاذكروني أذكركم}؛ فأمر تعالى بذكره، ووع: "So remember Me; I will remember you": He commanded His remembrance and promised the best reward for it, which is His remembering the one who remembers Him, as He said through His Messenger: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself, and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it". The best remembrance of Allah is that in which heart and tongue agree, the remembrance that bears knowledge of Allah, love of Him and abundant reward. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, so He commanded it specifically, then after it commanded gratitude in general, saying "and be grateful to Me" for the favours He bestowed and the afflictions He averted. Gratitude is by the heart through acknowledging favours, by the tongue through mention and praise, and by the limbs through obedience to Allah, submission to His command and avoiding His prohibition. In gratitude lies the preservation of existing favour and the increase of lost favour; the Exalted said "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you".
ثم حض المؤمنين على ما يوصلهم إلى الفلاح،: Then He urged the believers to what leads them to success, which is achieving happiness and triumph, and that the way leading to it is holding fast to patience, which is restraining the soul from what it dislikes: abandoning sins, enduring calamities and enduring commands heavy on souls; so He commanded them to be patient in all of that. Perseverance is constancy and continuing in it permanently and resisting enemies in all conditions. Vigilance is staying in the place from which enemy approach is feared, watching enemies and preventing them from reaching their aims, so that perhaps they succeed, that is, attain the religious, worldly and heavenly object of love and are saved from the disliked likewise. It is known from this that there is no way to success without the patience, perseverance and vigilance mentioned; whoever succeeded succeeded only by them, and no one missed success except by neglecting them or some of them.
هذه الآيات فيها حث الله عباده المؤمنين أ: These verses urge the believers to thank Allah for His great favours by fearing Him as He should be feared, upholding obedience to Him and leaving disobedience sincerely, establishing their religion and holding fast to His rope which He connected to them and made the link between them and Him, namely His religion and book, uniting upon it and not dividing, and persisting in that until death. He reminded them of their state before this favour, that they were scattered enemies, so He united them by this religion, joined their hearts and made them brothers, while they were on the brink of a pit of Fire and He saved them from wretchedness and led them to the path of happiness; therefore "Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may be guided", to thankfulness to Allah and holding fast to His rope.
فقوله تعالى: {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم}؛ أ: His words "Allah instructs you concerning your children": that is, your children, O parents, are with you as trusts that Allah has charged you with, to look after their religious and worldly interests, so you teach them, discipline them, restrain them from corruption, command them to obey Allah and to keep piety continually, as the Exalted said "O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones". Children are thus entrusted to their parents by counsel: either they uphold that counsel and have abundant reward, or neglect it and deserve warning and punishment. This shows that Allah is more merciful to His servants than parents are, since He gave parents a counsel despite their perfect compassion for their children.
هذا من لطفه تعالى بعباده وشكره للوالدين: This is from His kindness to His servants and His appreciation of parents: He enjoined children and entrusted them to treat their parents well, with gentle speech, soft words, spending money and maintenance and other forms of kindness. Then He pointed out the reason requiring it, recalling what the mother bore for her child and the hardship she endured during pregnancy, then the great hardship of labour, then the hardship of nursing and the care of raising; and these are not a brief time of an hour or two but a long period of "thirty months", nine months or so for pregnancy and the rest for nursing, which is the usual case.
أي: وأمرنا الإنسان ووصَّيْناه بوالديه حُ: That is: We commanded man and enjoined him concerning his parents with goodness, that is, to be dutiful to them and kind to them in word and deed, to keep to that, and not to disobey them or wrong them in word or deed; "and if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge": no one has any knowledge of the soundness of shirk, and this magnifies the matter of shirk; "do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do": so I will recompense you for your deeds. So be dutiful to your parents and give priority to obeying them, except over obedience to Allah and His Messenger, which takes precedence over everything.
{يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين}؛ أي: اخ: "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion": He selected it and picked it for you out of mercy and kindness to you, so uphold it, be characterised by its laws and take on the colour of its character until you continue upon that and death comes to you only while you are upon it, for whoever lives on something dies on it, and whoever dies on something is resurrected upon it.
أي: حُثَّ أهلك على الصلاة، وأزْعِجْهم إل: That is: urge your family to prayer and stir them to it, obligatory and voluntary; commanding something is commanding everything it cannot be completed without, so it is a command to teach them what makes prayer sound, invalid and complete. "And be steadfast therein": by establishing it with its limits, pillars, [etiquette] and humility, for that is hard on the soul, yet one should compel it and strive with it and be patient with it always; for when a servant establishes his prayer as commanded, he is more protective and upright regarding the rest of his religion, and if he neglects it, he is more negligent of everything else.
قوموا بلوازمه وشروطه، فَـ {قُوا أنفسكم و: Uphold its requirements and conditions, and "protect yourselves and your families from a Fire" described with these terrible descriptions; protecting oneself is by holding oneself to Allah's command in compliance and His prohibition in avoidance and repenting of what angers Allah and brings punishment, and protecting family and children is by disciplining them, teaching them and obliging them to Allah's command; so a servant is safe only if he upholds what Allah commanded in himself and in those under his charge, of wives, children and others who are under his authority and control …
ثم قال:{وعاشروهنَّ بالمعروف}: وهذا يشمل: Then He said: "and live with them in kindness": this includes kindness in word and deed; the husband must live with his wife in kindness, with good companionship, restraining harm, giving kindness and good treatment, including maintenance, clothing and the like, so the husband owes his wife what is customary for one like him toward one like her in that time and place, which varies with conditions. "And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good": that is, you husbands should keep your wives despite disliking them, for in that is much good, among it compliance with Allah's command and acceptance of His counsel, in which lies the happiness of this world and the next.
يأمر تعالى المؤمنين بتقواه في جميع أحوال: The Exalted commands the believers to fear Him in all their conditions, in secret and in public, and singles out and urges one aspect, upright speech, which is the speech that accords with what is right or comes close to it when certainty is unavailable, whether recitation, remembrance, enjoining good and forbidding evil, learning and teaching knowledge, striving to reach the right in matters of knowledge and following every path that leads to it and every means that helps it.
ثم أمر بالإحسان إلى الناس عموماً فقال:{و: Then He commanded kindness to people in general, saying "and speak to people good words": good speech includes commanding them to what is right, forbidding them from what is wrong, teaching them knowledge, extending greeting and cheerfulness and every other good word. Since a person cannot reach people with his wealth, he was commanded something by which he can be kind to every creature, which is kindness in speech; this includes the prohibition of foul speech to people, even to disbelievers, hence the Exalted said "and do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in the best way". Part of the manners with which Allah disciplined His servants is that a person be pure in his words and deeds, not vulgar, obscene, abusive or quarrelsome, but of good character and great forbearance, courteous to everyone, patient with the harm he receives from people, in compliance with Allah's command and hope for His reward.
هذه الآية جامعة لِحُسْنِ الخلق مع الناس: This verse is comprehensive of good character with people and how one should deal with them: what is fitting is to "accept forgiveness", that is, what their souls offer and what comes easily to them of deeds and character, so he does not burden them with what their natures do not permit, but is thankful for what anyone offers him of good word or deed or even less, overlooks their shortcomings, turns a blind eye to their deficiencies, is not arrogant toward the small for his smallness, the weak-minded for his weakness or the poor for his poverty, but treats everyone with gentleness and as the situation requires and as their hearts find pleasant. "And enjoin what is right": every good word, beautiful deed and complete character for near and far; so let what reaches people from you be teaching knowledge, urging good such as upholding kinship, dutifulness to parents, reconciling people, useful advice, sound opinion, help in righteousness and piety, deterring from evil or guiding to a religious or worldly benefit.
ثم أمر بإحسان خاصٍّ، له موقعٌ كبيرٌ، وهو: Then He commanded a particular kind of kindness of great weight, which is kindness to the one who wronged you, saying "Repel evil by that which is better": if one of people wrongs you, especially one with a great right upon you such as relatives and companions, by word or deed, meet it with kindness to him; if he cuts you off, keep ties with him; if he wrongs you, pardon him; if he speaks of you in your absence or presence, do not retaliate but pardon him and treat him with gentle speech; and if he shuns you and leaves addressing you, sweeten your speech to him and offer him greeting. When you meet evil with kindness, a great benefit results: "And thereupon the one between whom and you was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend", that is, as though he were a close, caring relative.
وهذا أيضاً من الآداب التي على أولي الألب: This too is among the manners that people of understanding must observe and apply: when a wrongdoer brings them news, they should verify his report and not take it at face value, for there is great danger and a falling into sin in that, because if his report were treated like that of a truthful, just person, a ruling would follow from it, causing loss of lives and property without right through that report, a cause of regret; rather, the duty upon a wrongdoer's report is verification and clarification …
وهذا أيضاً من حقوق المؤمنين بعضهم على بع: This too is among the rights of believers over one another: that "no people ridicule another people", by any speech, word or deed pointing to belittling the Muslim brother, for that is forbidden and impermissible and indicates the mocker's self-admiration; perhaps the one mocked is better than the mocker, which is the usual case and the reality, for mockery arises only from a heart full of bad character, adorned with every blameworthy trait and bare of every noble one; hence the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "It is enough evil for a man to belittle his Muslim brother". Then He said "and do not defame one another": do not find fault with one another; lamz is by speech and hamz by deed, and both are forbidden and carry the threat of Fire …
أي: أرشدِ المؤمنين وقُلْ لهم: الذين معهم: That is: guide the believers and tell them: those who have faith that prevents them from falling into what undermines faith should "lower their gaze", from looking at private parts, at unrelated women and at beardless youths, looking at whom is feared to cause temptation, and at worldly adornment that tempts and causes one to fall into what is to be avoided. "And guard their private parts": from unlawful intercourse in front or behind or less, and from allowing them to be touched or looked at.
يُرشد الباري عبادَه المؤمنين أن لا يدخُل: The Creator guides His believing servants not to enter houses other than their own without asking permission, for in that are several evils, among them what the Messenger, peace be upon him, mentioned when he said "Asking permission was made only because of the sight"; by neglecting it, the eye falls upon the private matters inside homes, for a home for a person in covering what is behind it is like a garment in covering the body.
ينهى تعالى عباده المؤمنين أن يأكلوا أموا: The Exalted forbids His believing servants to consume their wealth among themselves unjustly, which includes consuming it by usurpation, theft, gambling and bad earnings; perhaps it even includes consuming one's own wealth in extravagance and waste, since that is wrongful, not right. Then, having forbidden consuming it unjustly, He permitted them to consume it by trade and earnings free of obstacles and meeting the conditions of mutual consent and other things. "And do not kill yourselves": that is, do not kill one another, and let no one kill himself, which includes casting oneself into destruction and committing risks leading to loss and ruin. "Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you": part of His mercy is that He protected your lives and wealth and forbade wasting and destroying them and set what He set of penalties for it.
{إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا: "Indeed, those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah": the verse explains that the greatest cause of avoiding the forbidden usurious earnings is perfecting faith and its rights, especially establishing prayer and giving zakah, for prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing and zakah is kindness to creation, contradicting the practice of usury, which is injustice to them and harm toward them. Then He addressed the believers and commanded them to fear Him and give up what remains of the usurious dealings they used to practise before, and that if they do not do so they are waging war against Allah and His Messenger, which is among the greatest evidence of the abomination of usury, since He made the one who persists in it a warrior against Allah and His Messenger. Then He said "And if you repent", that is, from usurious dealings, "you may have your principal, not wronging", people by taking usury, "and not being wronged", by loss of your principal. So whoever repents of usury, if the dealings were past, he keeps what is past and his matter is left to Allah; if dealings are ongoing he must restrict himself to his capital, and if he takes an increase he has dared to take usury.
ومنها: أمره تعالى بكتابة الديون، وهذا ال: Among them: His command to write down debts. This command may be obligatory when preserving a right is obligatory, such as what a person holds in guardianship, like orphans' property, endowments, agents and trustees; it may approach obligation, as when the right belongs purely to an individual, and the obligation may be strong or the recommendation strong according to the circumstances. In every case writing is among the greatest means of preserving these deferred dealings because of frequent forgetfulness, the occurrence of false claims and to guard against traitors who do not fear Allah. Among them: His command to the scribe to write between the parties with justice, not inclining toward one because of kinship or otherwise nor against one out of enmity and the like. Among them: that writing between the parties is among the best deeds and a kindness to both, preserving their rights and clearing their obligations as Allah commanded him, so let the scribe seek reward in this among people.
هذا أمر من الله تعالى لعباده المؤمنين بم: This is a command from Allah to His believing servants, in what faith requires, to fulfil contracts, that is, to complete them and not break or reduce them. It includes the contracts between the servant and his Lord, taking on His servitude and upholding it perfectly without diminishing any of its rights; those between him and the Messenger through obeying and following him; those between him and parents and relatives through kindness to them, keeping ties and not severing them; those between him and his companions in upholding the rights of companionship in wealth and poverty, ease and hardship; and those between him and people, the contracts of dealings such as sale and hire and the like …
يحث الباري عباده على الإنفاق مما كسبوا ف: The Lord urges His servants to spend from what they earned through trade and from what He brought out of the earth for them of grains and fruits, which includes zakah on both currencies and all trade goods prepared for buying and selling and what comes out of the earth of grains and fruits. It includes the obligatory and the voluntary, and He commanded them to aim for the good of it and not aim for the bad, the worthless and poor which they offer to Allah though if the one who owed them a right gave them that, they would not accept it except by closing an eye. The duty is to give the average of these things, perfection is giving the best, and giving the worthless is forbidden since it does not suffice for the obligatory and does not bring the full reward in the recommended.
أي: فرض الله عليكم يا معشر المؤمنين {إذا: That is: Allah has prescribed upon you, O believers, "when death approaches one of you", that is, its causes, such as a fatal illness or approaching causes of destruction, and he "leaves wealth", meaning much wealth by custom, that he should bequeath to his parents and nearest relatives in fairness according to his means, without extravagance and without limiting it to the more distant to the exclusion of the nearer, but ranking them by nearness and need, which is why the comparative form was used here. His words "a duty upon the righteous" show its obligation, since a duty is what is established, and He made it among the requirements of piety.
هذا أول ما أوصى به من حقوق الخلق في هذه: This is the first thing He enjoined regarding the rights of creatures in this surah, namely the orphans who lost the fathers who sustained them while they are small and weak and cannot manage their own interests, so the Compassionate, Merciful commanded His servants to treat them well, not to approach their property except in the best way, to give them their property in full when they come of age and mature, and not to substitute the bad, which is consuming the orphan's property unjustly, for "the good", which is the lawful with no hardship or consequence, "and do not consume their property with your own", that is, together with your own, which warns of the ugliness of consuming their wealth in this state in which a person is already made independent by the provision Allah gave him; so whoever dares this has committed "a great sin", that is, a grave wrong and heavy burden. Part of substituting the bad for the good is that a guardian takes the orphan's precious property and puts his own worthless property in its place.
الأمانات كلُّ ما اؤتُمِنَ عليه الإنسان و: Trusts are everything a person is entrusted with and commanded to look after, so Allah commanded His servants to return them, that is, complete and full, not diminished, short-changed or delayed, and this includes the trusts of offices, wealth, secrets and the commands which only Allah knows.
يأمر تعالى عبادَه المؤمنين أن يكونوا {قو: The Exalted commands His believing servants to be "persistently standing firm in justice as witnesses for Allah"; qawwam is an intensive form, meaning be in all your conditions upholding justice, which is fairness in Allah's rights and in His servants' rights. Justice in Allah's rights means not using His favours against disobeying Him, but spending them in obeying Him; justice in people's rights means you give all the rights you owe as you demand your own rights, so you give the obligatory maintenance and debts and treat people as you would like them to treat you of character, repayment and other things.
أي: {يا أيُّها الذين آمنوا}: بما أمروا ب: That is: "O you who believe": in what they were commanded to believe in, uphold what your faith requires, by being "persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice": that your outward and inward movements be energised to uphold justice, that this standing be for Allah alone and not for any worldly aim, and that you aim at justice, neither excess nor deficiency in your words or deeds, and stand for it against the near and the far, the friend and the enemy. "And let not hatred of a people prevent you": that is, lead you "to be unjust" as one who has no justice or fairness does, but as you testify for your ally, testify against him, and as you testify against your enemy, testify for him, even if he is a disbeliever or an innovator; for justice toward him is obligatory and so is accepting the truth he brings, because it is true, not because he said it, and truth is not rejected because of who says it, for that is injustice to the truth.
{ولا تعاونَوا على الإثم}: وهو التَّجَرِّ: "And do not cooperate in sin": which is daring toward disobedience for which the doer is sinful and blameworthy, "and aggression": which is transgression against people in their blood, wealth and honour; every disobedience and wrong that a servant must restrain himself from, then help others abandon. "And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty": toward whoever disobeys Him and dares His prohibitions; so beware the prohibitions lest His punishment, immediate and delayed, befall you.
وأمرهم بتتميم هذه الحالة، والسبب الأقوى: He commanded them to complete this state, and the strongest means by which they can establish their religion is that a group among them, in whom there is sufficiency, take it upon themselves "to invite to good", which is the religion, its fundamentals, branches and laws, "and enjoin what is right", which is what is known to be good by law and reason, "and forbid what is wrong", which is what is known to be bad by law and reason; "and those are the successful", the ones who attain every aim and are saved from every fear. This group includes scholars and teachers, those engaged in preaching and admonishing people generally and specifically and those who hold people to account, who see to people establishing prayers, giving zakah and upholding the laws of the religion and forbid them wrongdoing. So everyone who calls people to good, generally or specifically, or gives general or particular advice, falls within this noble verse.
أي: ليكن دعاؤك للخلق مسلمهم وكافرهم إلى: That is: let your calling of creation, Muslim and disbeliever, to the straight path of your Lord, which comprises beneficial knowledge and righteous action, be "with wisdom", that is, each person according to his state, understanding, acceptance and compliance; part of wisdom is calling with knowledge, not ignorance, starting with the most important then the next, with what is nearest to minds and understanding and with what will be most fully accepted, and with gentleness and softness …
وقولُه:{فإن فاءتۡ فأصۡلِحوا بينَهما بالع: His words "then if it returns, make settlement between them with justice": this is a command to reconcile and to be just in the reconciliation, for reconciliation may exist but not with justice, rather with injustice and partiality to one of the two parties, and that is not the reconciliation commanded; so one must not favour either because of kinship, homeland or other aims that cause deviation from justice. "Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly": that is, those just in their judgment between people and in all the offices they hold, so that it even includes a man's justice with his family and dependants in fulfilling their rights; in the authentic hadith: "The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light: those who are just in their judgment, their families and what they are put in charge of".
ثم أمر بطاعتِهِ وطاعة رسولِهِ، وذلك بامت: Then He commanded obedience to Him and His Messenger, by complying with their commands, obligatory and recommended, and avoiding their prohibitions, and commanded obedience to those in authority, who are the rulers over people, the leaders, judges and muftis, for the matter of people's religion and worldly life cannot be set right except by obeying them and submitting to them, in obedience to Allah and desire for what is with Him, but on condition that they do not command disobedience to Allah; if they command it, there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator.
والتَّواصي بالحقِّ الذي هو الإيمان والعم: Counselling one another to truth, which is faith and righteous action, that is, they urge one another to it, encourage it and make it desirable. And counselling one another to patience in obeying Allah, in refraining from disobeying Allah and over Allah's painful decrees.
ثم فسَّر هذه العقبة بقوله: {فكُّ رقبةٍ}؛: Then He explained this steep path with His words "freeing a slave": freeing him from slavery by emancipating him or helping him pay his contract of manumission, and all the more so ransoming a Muslim captive from the disbelievers, "or feeding on a day of severe hunger", that is, great famine, by feeding at the time of need the most needy of people, "an orphan of near relationship", that is, combining being an orphan and poor and a relative, "or a needy person in dust", that is, one clinging to the dust from need and necessity.
