وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تن: Seek, through What Allah Gave You, the Home of the Hereafter, and Do Not Forget Your Share of the World
تنقل الآية نصيحة قوم قارون له: أن يبتغي: The verse relates the advice of Qarun's people to him: to seek the Hereafter through what Allah gave him, not to forget his share of the world and to do good as Allah did good to him.
وأما من بخل واستغنى: But as for Him Who Withholds and Considers Himself Free of Need
تقابل الآيات بين من أعطى واتقى فييسّر لل: The verses contrast one who gives and fears Allah, who is eased toward ease, with one who withholds and considers himself free of need, who is eased toward hardship and whose wealth will not avail him when he falls.
يأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل والذين يكنزون: Consuming People's Wealth Unjustly and Hoarding Gold and Silver
تحذّر الآيتان من أكل أموال الناس بالباطل: The two verses warn against consuming people's wealth unjustly and warn those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah of a painful punishment on the day it is heated in the fire of Hell.
الذي جمع مالاً وعدده يحسب أن ماله أخلده: Who Gathers Wealth and Counts It, Thinking That His Wealth Will Make Him Immortal
تصف الآيات الهمزة اللمزة بأنه جمع مالاً: The verses describe the slanderer as one who gathers wealth and counts it, thinking that his wealth will make him immortal, and warn that he will be thrown into the Crusher.
ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر: Rivalry in Worldly Increase Distracts You Until You Visit the Graves
توبّخ الآيات من شغلهم التكاثر حتى زاروا: The verses rebuke those whom rivalry in increase distracted until they visited the graves, affirm that they will know, and that they will be asked that day about pleasure.
وتأكلون التراث أكلاً لماً وتحبون المال ح: You Consume Inheritance Greedily and Love Wealth with Immense Love
تعدد الآيات من أحوال من لا يكرمون اليتيم: The verses list among the states of those who do not honour the orphan, do not urge feeding the poor, consume inheritance greedily and love wealth with immense love.
وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها: There Is No Creature on Earth but That Its Provision Is upon Allah
تقرر الآية أن رزق كل دابة في الأرض على ا: The verse establishes that the provision of every creature on earth is upon Allah, and that He knows its place of dwelling and its place of deposit.
وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون: In the Heaven Is Your Provision and What You Are Promised
تذكر الآية أن في السماء رزق الناس وما يو: The verse says that in the heaven is people's provision and what they are promised, and the next verse swears by the Lord of the heaven and earth that it is the truth.
إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله: If They Are Poor, Allah Will Enrich Them from His Bounty
تعد الآية الفقراء الراغبين في الزواج بأن: The verse promises poor people who wish to marry that Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and ends by saying that Allah is Vast and Knowing.
ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض: If Allah Were to Extend Provision to His Servants, They Would Transgress on Earth
تبين الآية أن بسط الرزق لعباده كلهم لأدّ: The verse shows that extending provision to all His servants would lead to transgression on earth, and that He sends it down in the measure He wills; He is Aware and Seeing of His servants.
الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء: Satan Threatens You with Poverty and Commands You to Immorality
تقابل الآية بين وعد الشيطان بالفقر وأمره: The verse contrasts Satan's threat of poverty and his command of immorality with Allah's promise of forgiveness and bounty.
إنما أوتيته على علم عندي: "I Was Given It Only because of Knowledge I Have"
تعرض الآيات قارون وقد آتاه الله كنوزاً ت: The verses present Qarun, to whom Allah gave treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men, the advice of his people and his reply that he was given it because of knowledge he had.
واضرب لهم مثلاً رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتي: Present to Them the Example of Two Men, One of Whom We Gave Two Gardens
تضرب الآيات مثلاً برجلين لأحدهما جنتان م: The verses give the example of two men, one with two gardens of grapevines, who said to his companion while conversing that he had more wealth and stronger men, and entered his garden while wronging himself.
ولهذا أخبر تعالى أنَّ المال والبنين {زين: Hence Allah informed us that wealth and children are "the adornment of worldly life", meaning there is nothing beyond that; and that what remains for a person, benefits him and gladdens him is the lasting good deeds. This includes all obligatory and recommended acts of obedience, of the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants: prayer, zakat, charity, Hajj and Umrah, glorification, praise, declaring His oneness, magnification, recitation, seeking beneficial knowledge, enjoining good and forbidding evil, joining kinship, dutifulness to parents, fulfilling the rights of wives, dependants and animals, and all forms of kindness to creation; all of this is among the lasting good deeds, and these "are better with Allah in reward and better in hope" …
أخبر تعالى في هاتين الآيتين عن حالة النا: In these two verses He informed us of people's state in preferring this world to the Hereafter, and made clear the great difference and wide gap between the two abodes. He told us that these things were made attractive to people, so they gazed at them with their eyes, found them lawful in their hearts and clung to their pleasures with their souls; each group of people inclines to one kind of these things and has made it its greatest concern and the limit of its knowledge, while it is, for all that, scanty enjoyment that ends in a short time: this is "the enjoyment of worldly life, while Allah has with Him the best return".
يأمر تعالى عبادَه بالإيمان به، وبرسوله و: He commands His servants to believe in Him, in His Messenger and in what he brought, and to spend in His cause from the wealth that Allah placed in their hands and made them successors over, so that He may see how they act.
وليست الأموال والأولاد {بالتي} تقرب إلى: Wealth and children are not what brings one near to Allah and draws one close to Him; what brings one near is faith in what the messengers brought and the righteous deed that is inseparable from faith. Those have the reward with Allah multiplied, each good deed ten times over up to seven hundred times and many more times that none knows but Allah.
ولما كان العبد ممْتَحَناً بأمواله وأولاد: Since a servant is tested through his wealth and children, and his love for them may lead him to put his own desire before fulfilling his trust, Allah informed us that wealth and children are a trial with which He tests His servants, and that they are a loan that will be returned to the one who gave it and given back to the one who entrusted it.
يأمر تعالى عباده المؤمنين بالإكثار من ذِ: He commands His believing servants to remember Him often, for in that is profit, success and abundant good, and forbids them to let their wealth and children distract them from remembering Him; for love of wealth and children is naturally in most souls, so they put them before love of Allah, and in that is great loss. Hence He said: "And whoever does that", meaning whoever is distracted by his wealth and child from the remembrance of Allah, "it is those who are the losers", of everlasting happiness and lasting bliss, because they preferred what perishes over what remains. He said: "Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward".
{ولا تُخۡزِني يَوۡمَ يُبۡعَثونَ}؛ أي: با: "And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected", that is, by rebuke for some sins, punishment for them and public shame; rather make me happy on that day on which neither wealth nor children will benefit "except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart": this is what benefits him with You, this is the one who is saved from punishment and deserves abundant reward.
أي: هو الذي سخَّر لكم الأرضَ وذَلَّلها؛: That is, He it is who subjected the earth to you and made it tractable, so that you may attain from it all that your need is attached to, of planting, building, tilling and roads by which one reaches distant regions and far-off lands; "so walk in its tracts", that is, to seek provision and earnings, "and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection": after you pass from this abode that Allah made a test and a means of provision for reaching the Hereafter, you will be raised after your death and gathered to Allah, who will recompense you for your good and bad deeds.
وهذا الأمر بترك البيع موقَّت مدَّة الصلا: This command to leave off selling is limited to the duration of the prayer; "then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land", to seek earnings and trade. Since busying oneself with trade is a likely cause of heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, Allah commanded remembering Him often, to make up for it, so He said: "and remember Allah often", that is, standing, sitting and lying on your sides, "that you may succeed": for increasing the remembrance of Allah is the greatest of the causes of success.
{وآخرون يضرِبون في الأرض يبتغونَ من فضل: "And others travel throughout the land seeking of Allah's bounty", that is: He knew that among you are travellers who travel for trade, so that they may be free of need of people and refrain from begging from them. The state of the traveller calls for lightening, which is why the obligatory prayer was lightened for him: he is permitted to combine two prayers in one time and to shorten the four-unit prayer.
هذا خطاب للناس كلهم مؤمنهم وكافرهم، فامت: This is an address to all people, believers and disbelievers alike. He reminded them of His favour by commanding them to eat of all that is on earth of grains, fruits and animals, as "lawful", meaning made lawful for you to take, not by seizure or theft, nor gained through a forbidden transaction or in a forbidden way, nor helping toward something forbidden, and "good", meaning not vile like carrion, blood, pork and all vile things.
أولئك؛ أي: المنافقون الموصوفون بتلك الصف: Those are the hypocrites described with those qualities, "who bought misguidance for guidance", that is, they desired misguidance as a buyer desires a commodity for which, from his desire for it, he pays precious wealth. This is one of the finest examples: He made misguidance, the utmost evil, like the commodity, and guidance, the utmost goodness, like the price; they paid out guidance, turning away from it, for misguidance, desiring it. This is their trade, and what an evil trade; this is their bargain, and what an evil bargain.
هذه وصيةٌ ودلالةٌ وإرشادٌ من أرحم الراحم: This is a counsel, a guidance and direction from the Most Merciful of the merciful to His believing servants toward the greatest trade, the most precious thing sought and the highest thing desired, by which one gains salvation from painful punishment and success in lasting bliss. He used the particle of offering, which indicates that this is something every patient person longs for and every wise person aspires to.
وإذا أردت أن تعرف مقدار الصفقة؛ فانظُرْ: If you want to know the size of the bargain, look at the buyer, who is he? He is Allah, Majestic is His majesty; and at the compensation, which is the greatest and most precious of compensations, the gardens of bliss; and at the price paid for it, which is self and wealth, the dearest of things to a person; and at the one through whose hands this sale was concluded, the noblest of messengers; and in which book was it written?
{ويلٌ}: كلمة عذابٍ وعقابٍ ، {للمطفِّفين}: "Woe", a word of torment and punishment, "to those who give less than due", and Allah explained those who give less as "those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full", meaning they take from them what is due to them from others, completely without deficiency, "but when they give by measure or weight", that is, when they give people their right due from them by measure or weight, "they cause loss", meaning they reduce it, either with a deficient measure and scale, or by not filling the measure and scale, or by other means; this is theft of people's wealth and injustice toward them.
{ويا قوم أوفوا المكيالَ والميزان بالقِسۡ: "And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice", that is, with the justice you would be pleased to be given, "and do not deprive people of their due", meaning do not reduce people's things, stealing them by taking with a deficient measure and scale, "and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption": for persisting in sins corrupts religion, beliefs, this world and the next, and destroys crops and offspring.
{والسماء رفعها}: سقفاً للمخلوقات الأرضيّ: "And the heaven He raised", as a roof for earthly creatures, "and He set up the balance", that is, justice between servants in words and deeds. By it is not meant the familiar scale alone, but as we mentioned it includes the familiar scale, the measure by which things are measured, the units by which unknowns are determined, and the truths by which creatures are distinguished and justice established among them. Hence He said: "that you not transgress within the balance", that is, Allah sent down the balance so that you do not exceed the limit in it; for if the matter returned to your minds and opinions, there would arise such disorder as Allah knows …
{الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا: "Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve": Allah will shade them in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His, give them good things and remove from them griefs, fears and hated things. His words "they will have their reward with their Lord", that is, each one according to his state, and specifying that it is with their Lord indicates the nobility of this state and that it falls in the greatest place, as in the authentic hadith: "A servant gives a date in charity from good earnings, and the Almighty accepts it in His hand and rears it for one of you as one of you rears his foal, until it becomes like a great mountain."
فأما الأول فإنه لما كانت نفقته مقبولة مض: As for the first, since his spending is accepted and multiplied, issuing from faith and complete sincerity, "seeking the pleasure of Allah and certainty within themselves", that is, they spend while firm, with generosity and truthfulness, the likeness of such a deed is "like a garden on a height", a raised place because it is exposed to the winds, the sun and the water, which is plentiful there; and if that heavy rain does not reach it, enough dew reaches it for the goodness of its soil and everything that supports its growth, flourishing and fruiting; hence "it brought forth its fruit in double", that is, multiplied. A garden of this description is the highest thing people seek, and this excellent deed is of the highest ranks.
يعني {لن تنالوا} وتدركوا {البر}، الذي هو: He means: "you will never attain" and reach "righteousness", which is a comprehensive name for good things and is the road that leads to Paradise, "until you spend from what you love", from the best and purest of your wealth. For spending from the good that souls love is among the greatest proofs of generosity of soul, its noble character, mercy and gentleness, and among the clearest proofs of love for Allah and of putting His love before love of the wealth to which souls are naturally strongly attached. Whoever prefers love of Allah to love of himself has reached the highest summit of perfection; and likewise whoever spends good things and does good to Allah's servants, Allah does good to him and grants him deeds and character that are not attained without this state.
قال تعالى لرسوله ومَنْ قام مقامه آمراً ل: Allah said to His Messenger, and whoever takes his place, commanding him with what purifies the believers and completes their faith: "Take from their wealth a charity", which is the obligatory zakat, "by which you purify them and cause them to grow", that is, purify them of sins and base character; "and cause them to grow" means to increase their good character and righteous deeds, increase their reward in this world and the next, and make their wealth grow; "and invoke blessings upon them", that is, pray for them, for the believers in general and specifically when they hand you the zakat of their wealth.
{وفي أموالهم حقٌّ}: واجبٌ ومستحبٌّ {للسا: "And in their wealth is a right", obligatory and recommended, "for the beggar and the deprived", that is, for the needy who ask people and those who do not ask them.
وتأمل هذا الحث اللطيف على النفقة وإن الم: Consider this gentle urging to spend, and that the one who spends has lent to Allah, the Rich and Generous, who promised him abundant multiplication, as He said: "The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed that grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains; and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is Vast and Knowing". Since the greatest obstacle to spending is fear of poverty, He informed us that wealth and poverty are in Allah's hand and that He withholds provision from whom He wills and extends it to whom He wills; so let one who wants to spend not hold back for fear of poverty, nor think that it is lost, for all servants return to Allah and those who spend and act will find their reward stored with Him when they need it most …
{ويطعِمونَ الطَّعامَ على حبِّه}؛ أي: وهم: "And they give food, in spite of love for it", that is, though they love wealth and food, yet they put love of Allah before love of themselves, and they seek out the most deserving and neediest, "the poor, the orphan and the captive", intending by their spending and feeding the face of Allah, saying in the tongue of their state: "We feed you only for the countenance of Allah; we wish not from you reward or gratitude", that is, no reward in wealth and no praise in words; "Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere", that is, very grim and evil, "distressful", that is, hard and narrow.
وإنَّما قدَّر الله هذا التقدير وحصر الفي: Allah ordained this measure and limited the spoils to these specified groups so that "it will not be a perpetual distribution", that is, circulating and monopolised, "among the rich among you". Had He not ordained it, the rich and strong would have exchanged it among themselves and the weak would have gained nothing from it, and in that is corruption known only to Allah; just as in following Allah's command and law are benefits beyond count. So He commanded the general rule and universal principle, saying: "And what the Messenger gives you, take; and what he forbids you, refrain from": this covers the roots of religion and its branches, outward and inward …
يعني أنه ينبغي أن تتحروا بصدقاتكم الفقرا: He means that you should seek out for your charity the poor who have confined themselves to the cause of Allah and to obedience to Him, who have no intention of earning or no ability for it, and who are so restrained that when an ignorant person sees them he thinks them wealthy; "they do not ask people persistently", so they do not ask at all, and if they ask out of necessity they do not press in asking. This kind of poor is the best place to put spending, to relieve their need, help them toward their aim and the path of good, and to thank them for the patience with which they are described and for looking to the Creator, not to creation …
يقول تعالى: {وآت ذا القُربى حقَّه}: من ا: The Exalted says: "And give the relative his right", of obligatory and recommended kindness and honour, a right that varies with circumstances, relatives, need or its absence, and times; "and the poor": give him his right from zakat and other than it, so that his poverty is lifted; "and the traveller", the stranger cut off from his land. All are given from wealth, in a way that does not harm the giver and does not exceed the fitting amount, for that is wastefulness, which Allah has forbidden, and He informed us that the wasteful are "brothers of the devils", because Satan calls only to every blameworthy trait, so he calls a person to miserliness and withholding; then if he disobeys him …
وقال هنا: {ولا تجعل يَدَكَ مغلولةً إلى ع: He said here: "And do not make your hand shackled to your neck", a metaphor for extreme withholding and miserliness, "and do not extend it completely", spending where one should not or more than one should, "so you would become" if you did that "blamed", that is, you would be blamed for what you did, "insolvent", that is, empty-handed: neither the wealth in your hand remains, nor does praise and commendation take its place.
{والذين إذا أنفَقوا}: النفقاتِ الواجبةَ: "And those who, when they spend", the obligatory and recommended expenditures, "are neither extravagant", exceeding the limit and entering the category of squandering, "nor niggardly", entering the category of miserliness and neglecting obligatory rights, "and it is between that", between extravagance and stinginess, "moderate": they spend on obligations such as zakat, expiations and obligatory maintenance, and on what is fitting, in the proper way without harm or reciprocal harm; and this is part of their justice and moderation.
ثم قال:{وكلوا واشربوا}؛ أي: مما رزقكم ال: Then He said: "And eat and drink", that is, of the good things Allah has provided you, "but be not excessive" in that. Excess is either exceeding the sufficient amount and greed for foods that harm the body, or increasing luxury and refinement in food, drink and clothing, or going beyond the lawful to the forbidden. "Indeed, He does not like the excessive": for Allah hates excess, and it harms a person's body and livelihood, so that it may even bring him to being unable to pay what is obligatory upon him of expenses.
أي: ولا يظن الذين يبخلون؛ أي: يمنعون ما: That is, let not those who are miserly, that is, who withhold what they have of what Allah gave them of His bounty, wealth, rank, knowledge and other things with which Allah favoured them and did good to them, and who commanded them to spend of it for His servants what does not harm them, but they were miserly with it, held it back and begrudged it to Allah's servants, thinking that it is good for them, whereas it is evil for them in their religion and worldly life, in the near and the far; "they will be encircled by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection", that is, what they were miserly with will be made a collar on their necks with which they are punished, as it came in the authentic hadith: "The miser's wealth will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald serpent with two black spots, taking him by his jaws, saying: I am your wealth, I am your treasure" …
{وابۡتَغ فيما آتاكَ الله الدارَ الآخرةَ}: "But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter", that is: you have gained of the means of the Hereafter, in wealth, what others do not have; so seek with it what is with Allah, give in charity, and do not limit yourself to merely attaining desires and gaining pleasures; "and do not forget your share of the world", meaning we do not command you to give all your wealth in charity and remain lost, but spend for your Hereafter and enjoy your worldly life in a way that does not breach your religion or harm your Hereafter; "and do good", to Allah's servants, "as Allah has done good to you" with this wealth, "and do not seek corruption in the land", through arrogance, disobedience to Allah and busying oneself with blessings to the neglect of the Giver.
{وأمَّا مَن بَخِلَ}: بما أمِرَ به، فترك: "But as for he who withholds", from what he was commanded, abandoning obligatory and recommended spending and whose soul was not generous in paying what is due to Allah, "and considers himself free of need", of Allah, leaving His worship aside and not seeing himself in utmost need of his Lord, with whom alone are its salvation, triumph and success, by His being its beloved and the one worshipped, to whom it turns, "and denies the best", that is, what Allah made it obligatory for servants to believe of good beliefs, "We will ease him toward difficulty", that is, toward the hard state and blameworthy traits, being eased toward evil wherever he is and assigned acts of disobedience.
{والذين يكنِزون الذَّهب والفضَّة}؛ أي: ي: "And those who hoard gold and silver", that is, hold them back, "and do not spend them in the way of Allah", that is, the paths of good that lead to Allah. This is the forbidden hoarding: to withhold them from obligatory spending, such as withholding zakat, or the obligatory maintenance of wives or relatives, or spending in the way of Allah when it becomes obligatory; "then give them tidings of a painful punishment".
ومن صفة هذا الهمَّازِ [اللَّمَّازِ] أنَّ: Among the qualities of this slanderer is that he has no concern except gathering wealth, counting it and delighting in it, and has no desire to spend it on the paths of good, on joining kinship and the like.
يقول تعالى موبِّخاً عباده عن اشتغالهم عم: The Exalted says, rebuking His servants for being busy with other than what they were created for, His worship alone without partner, knowing Him, turning to Him and putting love of Him before everything: "Diverted you", from that mentioned, "has competition in increase", without mentioning what they compete in, so as to include everything in which competitors compete and boasters boast, of [competition in] wealth, children, supporters, soldiers, servants, rank and other things in which each seeks to outdo the other, and for which the face of Allah is not the aim.
ولهذا قال:{وتأكُلون التُّراثَ}؛ أي: الما: Hence He said: "And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether", that is, wholesale, leaving nothing of it, "and you love wealth with immense love", that is, intense; and this is like His words: "But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting", "No! But you love the immediate and leave the Hereafter".
أي: جميع ما دبَّ على وجه الأرض من آدميٍّ: That is, all that crawls on the face of the earth, human, land or sea animal: Allah has taken on Himself their provision and sustenance, so their provision is upon Allah. "And He knows its place of dwelling and place of deposit", that is, He knows the dwelling place of these creatures, where they stay, settle and take shelter, and their place of deposit, where they move in their coming and going and in the accidents of their conditions.
وقوله: {وفي السماء رزقُكُم}؛ أي: مادة رز: His words "And in the heaven is your provision", that is, the source of your provision from rains and kinds of decrees, religious and worldly provision, and what you are promised of recompense in this world and the next; for it descends from Allah like all decrees.
وقوله:{إن يكونوا فقراءَ}؛ أي: الأزواج وا: His words "If they should be poor", that is, the spouses and those who marry, "Allah will enrich them from His bounty": so do not let what you imagine, that if he marries he becomes poor because of a large family and the like, hold you back. In it is an encouragement to marry and a promise to the one who marries of wealth after poverty.
ثم ذكر أن من لطفِهِ بعبادِهِ أنَّه لا يو: Then He mentioned that part of His kindness to His servants is that He does not widen this world for them with a breadth that harms their religion, so He said: "And if Allah had extended provision to His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the land", that is, they would have been heedless of obeying Allah and turned to enjoying worldly desires, which would have caused them to devote themselves to what their souls desire, even if it were disobedience and injustice. "But He sends down in due measure what He wills", according to what His kindness and wisdom require; "Indeed He is, of His servants, Aware and Seeing": as in some reports that Allah, the Exalted, says: "Among My servants are those whose faith is set right only by wealth, and were I to make him poor, that would corrupt it …
فلما حثهم على الإنفاق النافع نهاهم عن ال: When He had urged them to beneficial spending, He forbade them harmful withholding and showed that they are between two callers: the caller of the Most Merciful, who calls them to good and promises them good, bounty, reward in this world and the next and replacement of what they spent; and the caller of Satan, who urges them to withhold and frightens them that if they spend they will become poor.

حق السائل والمحتاج وحسن الرد: The asker's right and a kind reply
النهي عن نهر السائل، والأمر بالقول المعر: The prohibition of turning away the asker harshly, the command of a kind word and forgiveness, and that they are better than charity followed by harm.
إبطال الصدقة بالمنّ والأذى: Reproach and harm that spoil charity
النهي عن إبطال الصدقة بالمنّ والأذى وبيا: The prohibition of spoiling charity with reproach and harm, and the parable that shows it.
مدح الأنصار بحبهم من هاجر إليهم وإيثارهم: The praise of the Ansar for loving those who migrated to them and preferring them over themselves even when in need.
ذم الذين يمنعون الماعون، وهو ما جرت العا: The condemnation of those who withhold small kindnesses, the everyday things that are customarily lent or given.
أحكام المعاملات المالية من الآيات: الربا: The rulings of financial dealings from the verses: riba, sale, debt and contracts.
منزلة العمل والكسب وأمانة الكيل والوزن و: The standing of work and earning, honest measure and weight, and wages.
ما ذكره القرآن من المعادن والجواهر وما أ: The metals and gems the Quran mentions and what Allah brings out of the earth: iron, copper, gold, silver, pearl and coral; each passage with its verses in the Mushaf script and a verbatim quotation from the books of exegesis and hadith, with its meaning in English.
هذا الباب لما نصّ عليه القرآن من المعادن: This section is for what the Quran explicitly mentions of metals and gems and what is connected to them (their use, smelting, adornment, coinage, hoarding and the rulings on spending from them); it therefore does not repeat "Fruit and Food", "The Description of Paradise" or "Stories of the Prophets". The section titles and summaries are our concise wording of what the verses themselves indicate; what the exegetes said is attributed to them in the wording transmitted from the bundled books, and there is no scientific claim that is not quoted.
نصوص الآيات بلفظ مصحف المدينة النبوية (م: Verses are in the wording of the Madinah Mushaf (King Fahd Complex, version 18) and its script; the quotations are from the bundled books of exegesis and hadith in their own words, with bracketed words as in the original book, and a trailing ellipsis marks an excerpt cut from the sentence. What the exegetes say in explaining a word is theirs, not a ruling on the verse.
للحديد في القرآن سورة تحمل اسمه، وقد ورد: Iron has a surah named after it in the Quran. It appears as a favour and a source of strength, as a tool of work, as a figure of hardness and in the description of punishment; one place uses the word "hadid" as a description of sight rather than the metal, and it is pointed out.
آيات في صناعة الدروع وإقامة السدّ وصهر ا: Verses on making coats of mail, building the barrier and smelting metals in fire, with what the exegetes transmitted about how it was done.
القطر النحاس المذاب في تفسير المفسرين، و: Al-qitr is molten copper in the exegetes' explanation; copper appears in the description of punishment, together with the word "al-muhl", for which al-Qurtubi transmits several sayings, among them what is melted of the earth's substances.
الذهب والفضة: زينةً ونقداً وكنزاً: Gold and Silver: Adornment, Coinage and Hoarded Wealth
الذهب والفضة في القرآن زينة الدنيا وحُلي: In the Quran gold and silver are the adornment of this world, the ornaments of the people of Paradise and the money of people; the verses also warn against hoarding them without spending what is due.
جواهر نفيسة تُذكر في وصف النعمة والجمال،: Precious gems mentioned in describing blessing and beauty, some of them from the sea as the exegetes state; they are placed here for their closeness to gold and silver in describing adornment, not because they are minerals in the geological sense.
الأرض وما أُخرج منها: The Earth and What Is Brought Out of It
آيات فيما أودعه الله في الأرض وما يُخرجه: Verses on what Allah placed in the earth and brings out of it, and the related matters of spending, zakat and buried treasure in al-Qurtubi's words and the Sunnah.
إنزال الحديد: بأسٌ شديد ومنافع للناس: The Sending Down of Iron: Mighty Strength and Benefits for People
بعد ذكر الكتاب والميزان قال الله: «وأنزل: After mentioning the Book and the Balance, Allah says: "And We sent down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people, so that Allah may know who helps Him", joining the strength and usefulness of iron with the support of the religion.
ذكرت الآية الحديد في وصف عذاب الكافرين:: The verse mentions iron in describing the punishment of the disbelievers: "And for them are maces of iron".
أمر الله نبيه أن يقول للمنكرين للبعث: كو: Allah commanded His Prophet to say to those who denied resurrection: be stones or iron or some creation that is great in your minds. Iron is used as the figure of the hardest thing they can imagine, and He informs that He will bring them back as He began them.
فبصرك اليوم حديد (وصف للبصر لا ذكر للمعد: "Your Sight Today Is Sharp" (a Description of Sight, Not the Metal)
وردت لفظة «حديد» في قوله: «فبصرك اليوم ح: The word "hadid" occurs in "so your sight today is sharp" as a description of sight, meaning its keenness and strength, and not as a mention of the metal; it is listed here so that it is not counted as one.
ألنّا له الحديد: داود والدروع السابغات: We Softened Iron for Him: Dawud and the Full Coats of Mail
امتنّ الله على داود بأن ألان له الحديد،: Allah favoured Dawud by softening iron for him, commanding him to make full coats of mail and to measure the links in them, and to do righteous work.
صنعة لبوس لتحصنكم من بأسكم: The Craft of Armour to Protect You in Your Fighting
علّم الله داود صنعة الدروع وقاية للناس ف: Allah taught Dawud the craft of armour as protection for people in war, and the verse ends by asking about gratitude: "so will you be grateful?"
زبر الحديد والقطر: سد ذي القرنين: Sheets of Iron and Molten Brass: the Barrier of Dhul-Qarnayn
طلب ذو القرنين زبر الحديد حتى ساوى بين ا: Dhul-Qarnayn asked for sheets of iron until the gap between the two mountain-sides was levelled, ordered it blown upon until he made it fire, and poured molten brass over it, so the barrier became firm.
ومما يوقدون عليه في النار: مثل الحق والب: What They Heat in the Fire: the Parable of Truth and Falsehood
ضرب الله مثلاً بما يُوقد عليه في النار ا: Allah gives a parable from what is heated in fire seeking adornment or goods, which carries scum like the foam of water; it is a parable of truth that remains and falsehood that vanishes.
وأسلنا له عين القطر: And We Made a Spring of Molten Brass Flow for Him
أنعم الله على سليمان بأن أسال له عين الق: Allah favoured Sulayman by making a spring of "qitr" flow for him; al-Sa'di explains it as a spring of copper and the means made easy to extract from it.
شواظ من نار ونحاس: A Flame of Fire and Copper
ذُكر النحاس في وصف ما يُرسل على المكذّبي: Copper is mentioned in describing what is sent upon those who deny: "There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and copper, so you will not defend yourselves".
ماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه: Water Like the "Muhl" That Scalds the Faces
وصف الله شراب أهل النار بأنه «كالمهل يشو: Allah describes the drink of the people of Hell as "like muhl that scalds the faces"; the exegetes differ about the meaning of muhl, and al-Qurtubi transmits their sayings.
طعام الأثيم كالمهل: The Food of the Sinner Is Like the "Muhl"
شُبّه طعام الأثيم بالمهل يغلي في البطون: The food of the sinner is likened to muhl that boils in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water; al-Sa'di explains it here as foul pus of intense heat.
يوم تكون السماء كالمهل: On the Day the Sky Is Like the "Muhl"
شُبّهت السماء يوم القيامة بالمهل والجبال: On the Day of Resurrection the sky is likened to muhl and the mountains to carded wool; al-Sa'di explains muhl here as molten lead.
القناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة: Heaped-Up Hoards of Gold and Silver
جعل الله حب القناطير المقنطرة من الذهب و: Allah made the love of heaped-up hoards of gold and silver among the desires adorned for people, and the exegetes have sayings about the measure of a qintar.
القنطار والدينار في الأمانة: The Qintar and the Dinar in Trust
ذكرت الآية القنطار والدينار مثلين للكثير: The verse mentions the qintar and the dinar as examples of much and little wealth in trust and betrayal among the People of the Book.
أخبر الله أن الكافر لو افتدى بملء الأرض: Allah informs that were the disbeliever to ransom himself with the earth's fill of gold it would not be accepted from him; gold is the figure of the greatest thing one can give.
توعّد الله الذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا: Allah warns those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in His cause of a painful punishment, on the day it is heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, sides and backs are branded with it.
فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم: Send One of You with This Silver Coin of Yours
أرسل أصحاب الكهف أحدهم بورقهم إلى المدين: The companions of the Cave sent one of them with their "waraq" to the city to buy them food; al-Sa'di explains waraq as dirhams.
دراهم معدودة: ثمن يوسف: A Few Counted Dirhams: the Price of Yusuf
ذكرت الآية الدراهم المعدودة ثمناً بخساً: The verse mentions a few counted dirhams as the paltry price for Yusuf, peace be upon him.
أساور من ذهب في جنات عدن: Bracelets of Gold in the Gardens of Eden
وعد الله الصالحين بجنات عدن تجري من تحته: Allah promises the righteous the Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, where they are adorned with bracelets of gold and wear green garments of fine silk and brocade.
يُحلّى أهل الجنة بأساور من ذهب ولؤلؤ، ول: The people of Paradise are adorned with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments there are silk.
آنية من فضة وأكواب قوارير: Vessels of Silver and Goblets of Crystal-Clear Silver
يُطاف على أهل الجنة بآنية من فضة وأكواب: Vessels of silver and goblets that were crystal, crystal of silver, are passed around to the people of Paradise, which they measured exactly.
وصف الله أهل الجنة بأنهم «حلّوا أساور من: Allah describes the people of Paradise as "adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord gave them a pure drink".
يُطاف على أهل الجنة بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب،: Platters of gold and cups are passed around to the people of Paradise, containing whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, and they abide therein.
لولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعل الله ل: Were it not that people would be one community, Allah would have made for the houses of the disbelievers roofs of silver and stairways upon which they climb; that is only the enjoyment of worldly life.
أسورة من ذهب: قول فرعون: Bracelets of Gold: the Saying of Pharaoh
قال فرعون في موسى عليه السلام: «فلولا أل: Pharaoh said of Musa, peace be upon him: "Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him?", making ornament a sign of messengership.
يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان: From Them Come Pearl and Coral
من نعم الله في البحرين: «يخرج منهما اللؤ: Among Allah's favours in the two seas: "From them come pearl and coral".
كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان: As If They Were Ruby and Coral
شبّه الله نساء الجنة في صفائهن وجمالهن ب: Allah likens the women of Paradise in their purity and beauty to ruby and coral.
شبّه الله الحور العين باللؤلؤ المكنون ال: Allah likens the wide-eyed maidens to pearls concealed and guarded.
وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون: And We Caused to Grow in It Everything Weighed
من نعم الله في الأرض: «وأنبتنا فيها من ك: Among Allah's favours in the earth: "and We caused to grow in it everything weighed"; in al-Sa'di's exegesis, minerals are among what it includes.
وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها: And the Earth Brings Out Its Burdens
يوم القيامة تُخرج الأرض أثقالها، وفسّر ا: On the Day of Resurrection the earth brings out its burdens; al-Sa'di explains the burdens as what is in its belly of the dead and of treasures.
كنوز قارون ومفاتحه: The Treasures of Qarun and Their Keys
آتى الله قارون من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لت: Allah gave Qarun such treasures that their keys would burden a company of strong men, then his people advised him not to exult in his worldly wealth; the verse does not specify the kind of treasure, and al-Sa'di says they were treasures of wealth.
جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها: Streaks of White and Red of Varying Shades
من آيات الله في الجبال طرائق بيض وحمر مخ: Among Allah's signs in the mountains are streaks of white and red of varying shades and intensely black ones.
ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض: And from What We Brought Out for You from the Earth
أمر الله بالإنفاق من طيبات ما كسب المؤمن: Allah commanded spending from the good things the believers earn and from what He brought out for them from the earth; al-Qurtubi explains that what is brought out includes plants, minerals and buried treasure.
{إنَّ الله لَقَوِيٌّ عزيزٌ}؛ أي: لا يعجِ: Al-Sa'di: "Allah is Strong, Almighty": nothing overpowers Him and no fugitive escapes Him; and part of His strength is that He sent down iron, from which strong instruments come, and He is able to defeat His enemies, yet He tests His friends by means of their enemies to know who helps Him unseen. He joined the Book and iron in this place because by these two Allah supports His religion and raises His word: by the Book, which holds the proof, and by the sword that supports it with Allah's leave, both of them standing on justice and fairness.
وَقِيلَ: (أَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ) أَيْ أ: Al-Qurtubi: It was also said that "We sent down iron" means We brought it into being and created it, like the saying of Allah "and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock"; this is the saying of al-Hasan, so it would be from the earth, not sent down from the sky. And the people of meanings said: He brought iron out of the mines and taught them its craft by His revelation.
* * وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَأَنزلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ: Ibn Kathir: "And We sent down iron, in which is great might": We made iron a deterrent for whoever refuses the truth and is obstinate after the proof has been established against him; for this reason the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, stayed in Makkah thirteen years after prophethood while the Makkan surahs were revealed to him, all of them argument with the polytheists and clarification of tawhid with proofs; and when the proof had been established against whoever opposed Allah's law, He legislated the migration and commanded them to fight with swords.
أَعْطِهَا وَلَوْ خَاتَمًا مِنْ حَدِيدٍ: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Give her something, even an iron ring."
{ولهم مقامعُ من حديدٍ}: بيد الملائكة الغ: Al-Sa'di: "And for them are maces of iron": in the hands of the stern, mighty angels, who strike them with them and subdue them.
ولهذا أمر رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أ: Al-Sa'di: Hence He commanded His Messenger to say to those who deny resurrection out of disbelief: "Be stones or iron or some creation that is great in your breasts" so that you may, as you claim, be safe from Allah's power reaching you or His will taking effect in you; you cannot defeat Allah in whatever state you are or whatever form you change into, and you have no control over yourselves in life or after death; so leave management and control to the One who is over all things Competent and encompasses all things.
{فـ}: الآن {كَشَفۡنا عنك غِطاءَك}: الذي: Al-Sa'di: "So now We have removed from you your cover" which covered your heart so that your sleep grew long and your turning away continued, "and your sight today is sharp": it sees what disturbs and terrifies it of kinds of punishment and torment; or this is addressed by Allah to the servant, who in this world is heedless of what he was created for, but on the Day of Resurrection he wakes up and his drowsiness leaves him at a time when he can no longer make up for what he missed.
ومن فضله عليه أن ألانَ له الحديدَ؛ ليعمل: Al-Sa'di: Among His favour to him is that He softened iron for him so that he might make full coats of mail, and He taught him how to make them, by measuring it in the "sard", meaning to make it into rings and make it so, then to fit some into others; He said: "and We taught him the craft of armour for you to protect you in your fighting, so will you be grateful?" And when He mentioned what He had favoured him and his family with, He commanded them to give thanks and to do righteous deeds and to be mindful of Allah in it by keeping it right and guarding it from what spoils; for He is All-Seeing of their deeds, aware of them, nothing of them hidden from Him.
* * وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِ: Ibn Kathir: And His saying "and We softened iron for him": al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-A'mash and others said: he did not need to put it in fire or to strike it with a hammer; rather he twisted it with his hand like threads. Hence He said "Make full coats of mail", which are armours.
{وعلَّمۡناه صنعةَ لَبوسٍ لكم}؛ أي: علَّم: Al-Sa'di: "And We taught him the craft of armour for you", meaning Allah taught Dawud, peace be upon him, the craft of coats of mail; he was the first to make them and teach them and his craft spread to those after him; Allah softened iron for him and taught him how to link them, and the benefit in them is great: "to protect you in your fighting", meaning they are a shield and a safeguard for you in war and in the intensity of fighting.
يُحتمل أنَّ تعليم الله لداود صنعةَ الدُّ: Al-Sa'di: It is possible that Allah's teaching Dawud the craft of armour and the softening of it was a miracle beyond custom, and that it was as the exegetes said: Allah softened iron for him until he worked it like dough and clay without melting it in fire. And it is possible that His teaching him was according to the usual way and that the softening of iron for him was through the causes Allah taught him, which are known today for melting it, and this is the apparent meaning, because Allah gave this as a favour to people and commanded them to give thanks for it; and were his craft not among the things Allah made within the capacity of people, He would not have favoured them with it and mentioned its benefit; for the coats of mail Dawud made cannot be meant in their very selves, and the favour is in the kind.
{آتوني زُبَرَ الحديدِ}؛ أي: قطع الحديد،: Al-Sa'di: "Bring me sheets of iron", meaning pieces of iron, and they gave him that; "until, when he had levelled between the two mountain-sides" which the barrier was built between, "he said: Blow", meaning kindle the fire greatly and use bellows for it so that it intensifies and melts the copper; and when the copper he wanted to join between the sheets of iron melted, "he said: Bring me that I may pour over it molten brass", meaning molten copper; and he poured the molten brass over it, so the barrier became tremendously firm, and the people behind it were protected by it from the harm of Yajuj and Majuj.
وَالْقَطْرُ عِنْدَ أَكْثَرِ الْمُفَسِّرِ: Al-Qurtubi: Al-qitr, according to most exegetes, is molten copper; its origin is from "qatr" (dripping), because when melted it drips as water drips. And a group said: al-qitr is molten iron.
وَقَالَ الْعَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: Ibn Kathir: Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas on His saying "He sent down water from the sky and valleys flowed according to their measure, and the torrent carried a swelling foam": the torrent carried what was in the valley of wood and refuse; "and from what they heat in the fire" it is gold, silver, ornaments, goods, copper and iron; copper and iron have dross, so Allah made the parable of its dross like the foam of water; as for what benefits people, it is gold and silver, and what benefits the earth is what it drank of the water and so brought forth growth.
(ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ) أَيْ حِلْيَةِ الذَّ: Al-Qurtubi: "Seeking ornaments", meaning ornaments of gold and silver; "or goods, a foam like it": Mujahid said: iron, copper and lead.
لمَّا ذَكَرَ فضلَه على داود عليه السلام؛: Al-Sa'di: When He mentioned His favour to Dawud, peace be upon him, He mentioned His favour to his son Sulayman, peace be upon him: that Allah subjected the wind for him running at his command, carrying him and everything with him and covering a very long distance in a short time, travelling in a day the distance of two months: "its morning course a month", meaning from the start of the day till noon, "and its evening course a month", from noon till the end of the day; "and We made a spring of molten brass flow for him", meaning We made the spring of copper subject to him and made easy for him the means of extracting from it what is extracted of vessels and other things; and Allah also subjected to him the devils and the jinn, who could not disobey his command: "and whoever of them deviates from Our command, We make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze".
أي: {يرسَل عليكما} لهبٌ صافٍ من النار {و: Al-Sa'di: "There will be sent upon you" a pure flame of fire "and copper", which is the flame that smoke has mixed with. The meaning: these two dreadful things are sent upon you, O company of jinn and men, and surround you, so you will not defend yourselves, neither by help from yourselves nor by anyone who helps you apart from Allah.
{وإن يَسۡتغيثوا}؛ أي: يطلبوا الشراب ليطف: Al-Sa'di: "And if they call for relief", meaning ask for a drink to quench the severe thirst that befell them, "they will be relieved with water like muhl", meaning like molten lead or like the dregs of oil because of its intense heat.
وَقَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: هُوَ كُلُّ مَا: Al-Qurtubi: Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is everything melted of the earth's substances, of iron, lead, copper and tin, so it surges with boiling; that is the muhl.
فِي الصِّحَاحِ\" الْمُهْلُ\" النحاس المذ: Al-Qurtubi: In al-Sihah: "al-muhl" is molten copper. Ibn al-A'rabi: al-muhl is what is melted of lead. And Abu 'Amr said: al-muhl is the dregs of oil. And al-muhl is also pus and discharge.
لما ذَكَرَ يوم القيامة، وأنه يفصِلُ بين: Al-Sa'di: When He mentioned the Day of Resurrection and that He judges between His servants on it, He mentioned their division into two groups: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, who are the sinners by acts of disbelief and disobedience; and that their food is "the tree of Zaqqum", the worst and most hideous of trees, and that its food is "like muhl", meaning like foul pus, evil in smell and taste, intensely hot, "boiling in" their bellies "like the boiling of scalding water".
أي: {يوم} القيامة تقع فيه هذه الأمور الع: Al-Sa'di: That is, "on the day" of Resurrection when these tremendous things occur, "the sky will be like muhl", which is molten lead, from its splitting and the terror reaching it to the utmost, "and the mountains will be like carded wool", then after that they will become scattered dust and vanish.
وَقَدِ اخْتَلَفَ الْمُفَسِّرُونَ فِي مِق: Ibn Kathir: The exegetes differed on the measure of the qintar in several sayings, the sum of which is that it is abundant wealth, as al-Dahhak and others said; and it was said: a thousand dinars; and it was said: one thousand two hundred dinars; and it was said: twelve thousand; and it was said: forty thousand; and it was said: sixty thousand; and it was said: seventy thousand; and it was said: eighty thousand; and it was said other than that.
قَالَ الْعُلَمَاءُ: ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَا: Al-Qurtubi: The scholars said: Allah mentioned four kinds of wealth, each kind being held as property by a class of people: gold and silver are held by merchants, the marked horses by kings, livestock by people of the desert, and tilled land by people of the farmland.
الذَّهَبُ بِالذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةُ بِالْ: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, salt for salt, like for like, hand to hand; whoever gives more or asks for more has dealt in usury, the taker and the giver alike."
يخبر تعالى عن أهل الكتاب أن منهم طائفة أ: Al-Sa'di: Allah informs about the People of the Book that among them is a group who are trustworthy, so that if you entrusted them with qintars of money, meaning much wealth, they would return it to you, and among them is a group of traitors who betray you in the least of little things …
ثم إنه تعالى استثنى من هذا الوعيد التائب: Al-Sa'di: Then He excepted from this threat those who repent of their disbelief and sins, who set right their faults, for Allah forgives them what they put forward and pardons what they sent ahead; but whoever disbelieved and persisted in his disbelief, increasing only in disbelief until he died upon it, those are the ones who strayed from the path of guidance and followed the path of misery, and by this they deserved the painful punishment; they have no helper from Allah's punishment, and even if they gave the earth's fill of gold to ransom themselves, it would not benefit them at all.
وَأَمَّا الْكَنْزُ فَقَالَ مَالِكٌ، عَنْ: Ibn Kathir: As for hoarded wealth, Malik reported from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Umar that he said: it is the wealth from which zakat is not paid. And al-Thawri and others reported from 'Ubaydullah from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar: what has had its zakat paid is not a hoard even if it is under seven earths, and what is visible and has not had its zakat paid is a hoard; this was reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir and Abu Hurayrah, halting at them and attributed to the Prophet, and from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab similarly, may Allah be pleased with them: "Any wealth whose zakat you paid is not a hoard even if buried in the earth, and any wealth whose zakat you did not pay is a hoard with which its owner will be branded even if it is on the surface of the earth."
مَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ ذَهَبٍ وَلاَ فِضَّةٍ لا: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "No owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due from it but, on the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be beaten out for him and heated in the fire of Hell, and with them his side, his forehead and his back will be branded; whenever they cool they are returned to him, in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgement is passed between the servants, and he sees his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire."
ثم إنَّهم لما تساءلوا بينهم، وجرى منهم م: Al-Sa'di: Then, when they had questioned one another and what Allah reported had passed between them, they sent one of them with their "waraq", meaning the dirhams they had with them …
وكان إخوته قريباً منه، فاشتراه السيارةُ: Al-Sa'di: His brothers were near him, and the travellers bought him from them "for a paltry price", meaning very little, which He explained by His saying "a few counted dirhams, and they were of those who held him cheap" …
ودلت الآية الكريمة وما أشبهها على أن الح: Al-Sa'di: This verse and its like show that ornament is general for males and females, as reported in the sound reports, because He used the general wording "they will be adorned", and likewise silk and the like.
والعَدْنُ: الإقامة؛ فجنات عدنٍ؛ أي: جنات: Al-Sa'di: "Adn" means residence, so the Gardens of Adn are gardens of residence; He attributed them to residence because residence and eternity are their description and the description of their people; "they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold", which is the ornament put on the arms in the way they love and see to be finer than another; men and women are equal in ornament in Paradise; "and pearls" strung into their garments and bodies, "and their garments therein will be silk", of fine silk and green brocade.
{ويُطافُ عليهم}؛ أي: يدور الولدان والخدم: Al-Sa'di: "And there will be passed around" among them, meaning the boys and servants circle among the people of Paradise, "vessels of silver and goblets that were crystal, crystal of silver", meaning their substance is silver while having the clarity of crystal, and this is among the most wondrous things, that dense silver has, from the clarity of its essence and goodness of its mine, the clarity of crystal; "they measured them exactly", meaning they measured the mentioned vessels to the measure of their quenching, neither more nor less, because were it more, its pleasure would lessen, and were it less, it would not suffice their quenching.
الَّذِي يَشْرَبُ فِي آنِيَةِ الْفِضَّةِ: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The one who drinks from vessels of silver is only making the fire of Hell gurgle in his belly."
{عاليهم ثيابُ سندسٍ خضرٌ}؛ أي: قد جلَّلت: Al-Sa'di: "Upon them will be garments of green fine silk", meaning they are covered with garments of sundus and istabraq, green, which are the finest kinds of silk, sundus being the thicker silk and istabraq the thinner, "and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver" …
{يطافُ عليهم بصحافٍ من ذهبٍ وأكوابٍ}؛ أي: Al-Sa'di: "Platters of gold and cups will be passed around them", meaning their servants, the immortal boys, circle among them with their food in the finest and noblest vessels, which are the platters of gold, and with their drink in the gentlest vessels, which are the cups that have no handles, among the clearest of vessels, of silver clearer than crystal, "and therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in": this wording is comprehensive and comes upon every bliss, joy, comfort of the eye and delight of the heart; everything the souls desire of food, drink, clothing and marriage, and the eyes delight in of beautiful sights, encircling trees, lovely blessings and adorned buildings is present there, prepared for its people in the most complete and best way, as He said: "They will have fruit therein, and they will have whatever they ask for".
لاَ تَلْبَسُوا الْحَرِيرَ وَلاَ الدِّيبَ: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Do not wear silk or brocade, and do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat from their plates, for they are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter."
يخبر تعالى بأنَّ الدُّنيا لا تسوى عنده ش: Al-Sa'di: Allah informs that the world is worth nothing with Him, and that were it not for His kindness and mercy to His servants, which nothing precedes, He would have expanded the world greatly for those who disbelieved and would have made "for their houses roofs of silver and stairways", meaning steps of silver, "upon which they climb" to their rooftops, "and for their houses doors and couches upon which they recline", of silver, and would have made for them "gold adornment", meaning He would have adorned their world for them with kinds of ornaments and given them what they desire, but His mercy to His servants prevented that, fearing for them hastening into disbelief and many sins because of the love of the world. In this is evidence that He withholds from servants some worldly things, generally or specifically, for their interests, and that the world does not weigh the wing of a gnat with Allah.
ثم قال فرعونُ: {فلولا ألۡقِيَ عليه أسورة: Al-Sa'di: Then Pharaoh said: "Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him?", meaning: why was Musa not in this state, adorned and beautified with ornaments and bracelets, "or angels come with him in company": helping him in his call and supporting him in his word.
المراد بالبحرين: البحر العذب والبحر الما: Al-Sa'di: What is meant by the two seas is the fresh sea and the salt sea; they meet, the fresh pouring into the salt and mixing and blending, but Allah placed between them a barrier of earth so that neither transgresses on the other and benefit is gained from each: from the fresh they drink and their trees, crops and tillage drink, and by the salt the air becomes pleasant and fish and pearl and coral are generated …
{فيهنَّ قاصراتُ الطرفِ}؛ أي: قد قصرنَ طر: Al-Sa'di: "In them are maidens restraining their glances", meaning they restrain their glances for their husbands out of their husbands' beauty and their own perfect love for them, and they also restrain their husbands' glances to themselves by their beauty, the pleasure of union with them and the intensity of their love; "whom no man has touched before them, nor jinn", meaning no one before them of men or jinn has reached them, but they are virgins, loving, endearing to their husbands by good companionship, coquetry, charm and daintiness; hence He said "as if they were ruby and coral", for their clarity, the beauty of their appearance and their radiance.
{كأمثال اللُّؤلؤ المكنونِ}؛ أي: كأنَّهن: Al-Sa'di: "Like pearls well guarded", meaning as if they were white, fresh, clear, radiant pearl, hidden from eyes, wind and sun, whose colour is among the finest of colours, with no flaw in any respect; so are the wide-eyed maidens, no flaw in them in any respect, but perfect in attributes and beautiful in description; everything you contemplate of them, you find only what delights the heart and pleases the eye.
{وأنبَتۡنا فيها من كلِّ شيءٍ موزونٍ}؛ أي: Al-Sa'di: "And We caused to grow in it everything weighed", meaning beneficial and well measured, which servants and lands need, among palms, grapes, kinds of trees, kinds of plants and minerals.
يخبر تعالى عمَّا يكون يوم القيامة، وأنَّ: Al-Sa'di: Allah informs about what will be on the Day of Resurrection: the earth will shake, quake and tremble until what is on it of buildings and landmarks falls, its mountains crumble, its hills are levelled and it becomes a level plain with no crookedness or unevenness in it; "and the earth brings out its burdens", meaning what is in its belly of the dead and of treasures …
يخبر تعالى عن حالة قارون وما فَعَلَ وفُع: Al-Sa'di: Allah informs of the state of Qarun and what he did, what was done to him, and how he was advised and admonished: "Indeed Qarun was of the people of Musa", meaning of the Children of Israel, who excelled the worlds and surpassed them in their time, and Allah favoured them with what He favoured them; their state was suited to uprightness, but this Qarun transgressed against his people and tyrannised by the great, tyranny-inducing wealth he was given; "and We gave him of the treasures", meaning treasures of wealth, a great deal, "whose keys would burden a company of strong men": a company is from ten to nine to seven or so, meaning the keys of his treasuries of wealth weighed down the strong group from carrying them; so what do you think of the treasuries? "When his people said to him", advising him and warning him against tyranny: "Do not exult; indeed Allah does not like the exultant", meaning do not exult in this great world and boast of it so that it distracts you from the Hereafter; for Allah does not like those who exult in it and are absorbed in loving it.
ومن ذلك الجبالُ التي جعلها الله أوتاداً: Al-Sa'di: And among that are the mountains which Allah made pegs for the earth; you find them interlocked mountains, indeed one mountain, with many colours in it: "streaks of white", meaning white tracts, and in them are tracts of yellow and red, and "intensely black ones", meaning extremely black.
الرَّابِعَةُ- قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمِمّ: Al-Qurtubi: The fourth: His saying "and from what We brought out for you from the earth" means plants, minerals and buried treasure, and these are three chapters this verse contains.
قَالَ عُلَمَاؤُنَا: لَمَّا قَالَ ﷺ: \"وَ: Al-Qurtubi: Our scholars said: when the Prophet, peace be upon him, said "and in buried treasure is the fifth", it indicated that the ruling on minerals differs from the ruling on buried treasure, because he separated minerals and buried treasure with the conjunction; had the ruling been the same, he would have said "the mine is without liability and in it is the fifth"; so when he said "and in buried treasure is the fifth", it was known that the ruling on buried treasure differs from the ruling on the mine in what is taken from it, and Allah knows best. And "rikaz" originally in the language is what is embedded in the earth of gold, silver and gems, and it is so among all the jurists, because they say about the nugget found in the mine embedded in the earth, not obtained by work, effort or toil, that the fifth is due on it, because it is rikaz.
الْعَجْمَاءُ جُبَارٌ، وَالْبِئْرُ جُبَار: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The beast's injury is without liability, the well is without liability, the mine is without liability, and in buried treasure is the fifth."
يتتبّع هذا الباب لفظ «الرجال» ووصف الله: This chapter follows the word "men" and how Allah describes men in the Quran by their social and moral qualities: faithfulness, steadfastness, remembrance, counsel, speaking the truth and responsibility in the community. The stories of non-prophet men belong to "The man's corner in the Quran"; family rulings and responsibilities belong to "The family corner" and "Marriage and divorce"; and this chapter is not a general survey of the traits of faith.

صفات الرجال في القرآن: Qualities of men in the Quran
الصفات التي وصف الله بها الرجال في القرآ: The qualities with which Allah described men in the Quran in their social and moral being: faithfulness to the pledge, steadfastness, remembrance, counsel, speaking the truth and responsibility in the community, with their parables and their youths; the verses in Mushaf script and the exegetes' words verbatim, with an English meaning for each.

الآيات التي وصفت رجالاً صدقوا ما عاهدوا: The verses describing men who were true to what they pledged to Allah, who spoke the word of truth where there was fear, and believers who lived among the polytheists.

الآيات التي وصفت رجالاً يسبّحون الله في: The verses describing men who glorify Allah in the mosques whom trade does not distract, who love to purify themselves, and who come to the House from every distant pass.
