أسماء الله الحسنى وصفاته: The Beautiful Names and Attributes of Allah
كل اسم ورد لفظه في القرآن، وصفات الله ال: Every name whose wording occurs in the Quran, and the lofty attributes of Allah, with their verses, meanings and explanation in the exact words of the commentators, plus the hadiths on the names and attributes with their sources and grades.
كل اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى جاء لفظه في: Every beautiful name of Allah whose wording occurs in the Noble Quran, and His lofty attributes as He affirmed them for Himself in His Book: with their verses in the Mushaf script, their meanings, and their explanation in the exact words of the commentators, following the Sunni approach: affirmation without asking how, without likening and without denial.
والأسماء الحسنى لا تنحصر في عدد، وهذا ال: The beautiful names are not limited to a number, and this section keeps to what occurs in the Quran in wording. The attribute chapters affirm what Allah affirmed for Himself in His Book; they do not delve into how, nor into disputed matters of theology. Al-Qurtubi's reinterpretations of the attributes are not quoted, because the approach here is that of the Salaf. The attribute chapters quote al-Saadi, Ibn Kathir and al-Baghawi, and the hadiths are from the two Sahihs.
الطب والشفاء في القرآن الكريم: Medicine and Healing in the Noble Quran
ما أشار إليه القرآن الكريم من أسباب الصح: What the Noble Quran indicates about the causes of health and illness, honey, food, fasting, mental wellbeing, purity, pregnancy and breastfeeding, each passage with its verses in the Mushaf script, a verbatim quotation from the books of exegesis and authentic hadiths in their own wording.
هذا الباب بيان لما أشار إليه القرآن والس: This chapter explains what the Quran, the authentic Sunnah and the exegetes' statements indicate. It is not a medical book, a prescription or a substitute for a doctor. What it mentions of honey, dates or other things is reported from the exegetes and is not a scientific claim, so no treatment is to be abandoned nor a doctor delayed because of it. In illness and severe symptoms consult a qualified doctor.
هذا الباب في الإشارات الصحية والغذائية و: This chapter concerns the health, dietary and psychological indications in the Quran. It differs from "Diseases and Treatment in the Quran" (an index of verses on illness and treatment), from "Healing by the Quran" (the lawful ruqyah) and from "Scientific Miracles". The titles and summaries are our wording of what the verses indicate, while the verses, the exegetes' statements and the hadiths are in their own words from the bundled sources; nothing is attributed to Allah, His Messenger or an exegete except what they stated.
نصوص الآيات بلفظ مصحف المدينة النبوية (م: Verses are in the wording of the Madinah Mushaf (King Fahd Complex, version 18) and its script; quotations from the books of exegesis and hadiths from the Six Books are in their own words from the bundled sources, and a trailing ellipsis marks an excerpt cut from the sentence. This chapter is no substitute for a doctor.
الشفاء من الله والأخذ بالأسباب: Healing Comes from Allah, with Taking the Means
أصل الباب: المرض والشفاء بقضاء الله وقدر: The foundation of the chapter: sickness and healing are by the decree of Allah, yet the Law commands seeking treatment, taking precautions and preserving life. Here are the Quranic passages on this, with the authentic hadiths that explain them.
الموضع الوحيد الذي نصّ فيه القرآن على «ش: The only place where the Quran states "healing for people" in a drink that comes out of the bee. The exegetes differ over what the pronoun refers to and over how general the healing is, so the disagreement is given in their own words.
آيات الأكل والشرب: الإباحة والاعتدال وال: Verses on eating and drinking: permissibility, moderation and wholesome things, what Allah forbade of foul things and intoxicants, and what the exegetes mentioned of their benefit or harm.
الصيام فريضة وعبادة، ومعه رخصة المريض في: Fasting is an obligation and an act of worship, and with it comes the sick person's concession to break the fast. We give what the exegetes said of its wisdom in their own words, without attributing to them medical benefits they did not state.
الصحة النفسية وشفاء الصدور: Mental Wellbeing and the Healing of Hearts
ما في القرآن مما يتصل بالطمأنينة والسكين: What the Quran says that bears on tranquillity, calm, grief, hope, patience, sleep and trust in Allah: what strengthens the heart and removes anxiety, in the words of the verses and the exegetes.
أمر القرآن بالطهارة ومدح المتطهرين، وسمّ: The Quran commands purification, praises those who purify themselves, calls menstruation "an impurity" and makes water purifying. We give the exegetes' account of these aims.
ما ذكره القرآن من أحوال الحمل والرضاعة و: What the Quran mentions of pregnancy and breastfeeding and their durations, what the mother bears, and what the exegetes derived from it.
قالها إبراهيم عليه السلام: نسب المرض إلى: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said it: he ascribed the illness to himself and the healing to Allah alone, so healing is in Allah's hand. The authentic hadiths confirm that every disease has a cure and that seeking treatment is lawful.
اركض برجلك: سبب الشفاء من الله: Strike with Your Foot: A Means of Healing from Allah
أمر الله أيوب عليه السلام بأن يضرب الأرض: Allah commanded Ayyub, peace be upon him, to strike the earth with his foot, whereupon a spring gushed out from which he washed and drank; the story ends with "We found him patient". Healing is from Allah and comes with the servant taking the means that are provided for him.
الحذر مع التوكل: ادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة: Caution with Trust: Enter by Different Gates
وصّى يعقوب عليه السلام أبناءه بأخذ سبب ا: Yaqub, peace be upon him, advised his sons to take the means of caution, then returned the whole matter to Allah: "In Him I put my trust". He joined the means with trust. In the hadith, the Bedouins asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, "Shall we seek treatment?" and he commanded them to do so.
نهى الله عن إلقاء النفس إلى الهلاك، وفسّ: Allah forbade casting oneself into ruin; al-Sa'di explained that as leaving what the servant is commanded when that leads to the destruction of the body, and doing what leads to the ruin of the self. From here the scholars established that preserving life is one of the aims of the Law.
نهى الله المؤمنين عن قتل أنفسهم، وبيّن ا: Allah forbade the believers to kill themselves, and al-Sa'di explained that this includes casting oneself into destruction and taking dangerous risks that lead to ruin. In the Sunnah: caution about plague, so one does not enter a land where it is nor leave it, and the sick are not brought to the healthy.
يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه: From Their Bellies Comes a Drink of Varying Colours
ذكر الله وحيه إلى النحل وما يخرج من بطون: Allah mentions His inspiration to the bee and what comes out of its belly: a drink of varying colours in which is healing for people. The exegetes mention Allah's care for it and the variety of honey by pasture, and in the two Sahihs the Prophet, peace be upon him, ordered honey for one who complained of his stomach.
فيه شفاء للناس: إلى أي شيء يعود الضمير؟: In It Is Healing for People: What Does the Pronoun Refer To, and Is the Healing General?
قال الجمهور: الضمير للعسل. ورُوي عن ابن: The majority said: the pronoun refers to honey. It is related from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Mujahid that it refers to the Quran, and Ibn al-Arabi rejected that. Then they differed: is its healing general for every ailment and every person, or is it a medicine that benefits in some conditions and not others? We give both views in al-Qurtubi's words; this is one example of why the verse is not turned into a general medical prescription.
Allah made eating and drinking lawful and forbade excess. Al-Sa'di explained excess as exceeding the sufficient amount in foods that harm the body, and al-Qurtubi reported what was said of the benefits of eating little and the harms of eating much, and cited the hadith "The son of Adam fills no vessel worse than his stomach".
كلوا من الطيبات حلالاً طيباً: Eat of the Good Things, Lawful and Wholesome
أمر الله الناس بالأكل مما في الأرض حلالا: Allah commanded people to eat of what is in the earth, lawful and good, and al-Sa'di noted that the basic rule is permissibility and that the forbidden is of two kinds: what is forbidden in itself, namely the foul, and what is forbidden for an incidental reason.
ذكر الله اللبن من نعمه: يخرج من بين فرث: Allah mentions milk among His favours: it comes out from between dung and blood as pure milk, pleasant for those who drink. Al-Qurtubi relates from the scholars that it is the first thing a human is nourished by and by which bodies grow.
جعل الله الماء أصل الحياة: السماء بالمطر: Allah made water the origin of life: the sky through rain and the earth through vegetation. This is a verse on the origin of food and drink, for from this water come food and drink for every living thing.
شجرة الزيتون: دهن وصبغ للآكلين: The Olive Tree: Oil and Condiment for Those Who Eat
ذكر الله شجرة الزيتون التي تنبت بالدُّهن: Allah mentions the olive tree that grows with oil and a condiment for those who eat, and al-Sa'di pointed to its benefits: oil for lighting and as an accompaniment to food.
هزّي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطباً ج: Shake the Trunk of the Palm Tree toward You: Fresh Ripe Dates
أمر الله مريم عليها السلام وهي في حال ال: Allah commanded Maryam, peace be upon her, while in labour, to shake the trunk of the palm tree so that fresh dates would fall upon her. Al-Qurtubi reported from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym that fresh dates are the best thing for a woman after childbirth because of this verse, and mentioned that dates became a custom for women after childbirth; this is a statement of a scholar, not a hadith.
حُرّمت الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير: Forbidden to You Are Carrion, Blood and Swine
حرّم الله الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما: Allah forbade carrion, blood, the flesh of swine and what is dedicated to other than Allah. Al-Sa'di explained that Allah forbids only to protect His servants from the harm that exists in the forbidden things, whether He makes it clear or not, and he explained the harm of carrion in his own words.
الخمر والميسر: إثم كبير ومنافع للناس: Wine and Gambling: Great Sin and Some Benefits for People
ذكر الله أن في الخمر والميسر «إثم كبير و: Allah said that in wine and gambling there is "great sin and some benefits for people", and that their sin is greater than their benefit, then forbade them in al-Ma'idah. Al-Sa'di explains what comes from wine of loss of reason, wealth and enmity, and this was Allah's kindness in making the prohibition gradual.
كُتب عليكم الصيام لعلكم تتقون: Fasting Is Prescribed for You That You May Become Righteous
فرض الله الصيام وبيّن حكمته: «لعلكم تتقو: Allah prescribed fasting and explained its wisdom: "that you may become righteous". Al-Sa'di quoted several aspects: leaving food and drink to draw near to Allah, being watchful of Allah, narrowing the devil's channels, more obedience and sympathy with the poor. The wisdom stated is piety of the heart, and the exegete says nothing here about its medical benefits.
يريد الله بكم اليسر: رخصة المريض: Allah Intends Ease for You: The Concession for the Sick
رخّص الله للمريض والمسافر في الفطر ثم ال: Allah allowed the sick and the traveller to break the fast and make it up later, and closed with "Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship". This is a basis for taking account of bodily ailment: the obligation is lifted where it would cause harm, and the detailed rulings on the sick person and fasting are in the chapter on fiqh.
جعل الله ذكره سبب طمأنينة القلوب. وفسّر: Allah made His remembrance a cause of the heart's peace. Al-Sa'di explained peace as the vanishing of anxiety and agitation, and said that nothing is sweeter to hearts than love of their Creator and intimacy with Him.
قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الص: There Has Come to You an Admonition from Your Lord and a Healing for What Is in the Breasts
Allah described the Quran as a healing for what is in the breasts. Al-Sa'di explained it as healing the diseases of desires and the diseases of doubts, and al-Baghawi as a remedy for ignorance. This is healing of hearts; ruqyah by the Quran has its own chapter in "Healing by the Quran".
هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين: It Is He Who Sent Down Tranquillity into the Hearts of the Believers
ذكر الله أنه أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمن: Allah mentions that He sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers. Al-Sa'di explained that it is calm, peace and steadfastness in disquieting trials that disturb hearts and weaken souls.
ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا: Do Not Weaken and Do Not Grieve
خاطب الله المؤمنين بعد الهزيمة: «ولا تهن: Allah addressed the believers after the defeat: "Do not weaken and do not grieve". Al-Sa'di explained that grief in the heart and weakness in the body are an added calamity, and commanded them to encourage their hearts and drive grief away.
بشّر الله بأن اليسر يصاحب العسر ويقارنه،: Allah gave the good news that ease accompanies hardship and goes with it, and al-Sa'di explained the eloquence of the wording, that ease is repeated while hardship is one. This is a basis of hope and a remedy for despair.
ولا تيأسوا من روح الله: Do Not Despair of the Mercy of Allah
قالها يعقوب عليه السلام لبنيه وهو في حزن: Yaqub, peace be upon him, said it to his sons while in deep grief: there is no despair where there is hope. Al-Sa'di explained that hope calls for effort and striving, while despair calls for heaviness and slowness.
لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله: Do Not Lose Hope in the Mercy of Allah
نادى الله عباده المسرفين على أنفسهم: «لا: Allah called His servants who have transgressed against themselves: "Do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah". Al-Sa'di explained despair as the giving up that casts its owner into ruin.
ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى: We Did Not Send Down the Quran upon You to Cause You Distress
نفى الله أن يكون القرآن لشقاء العبد، وفس: Allah denied that the Quran is for the servant's distress, and al-Sa'di explained that it was legislated as mercy, made as easy as possible and made food for hearts and souls and rest for bodies.
ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع … وبشر ال: We Will Surely Test You with Some Fear and Hunger … and Give Good Tidings to the Patient
أخبر الله أنه يبتلي عباده بالخوف والجوع: Allah said He tests His servants with fear, hunger and loss of wealth, lives and fruits, and gave glad tidings to the patient. Al-Sa'di explained the state of the patient and the impatient, and that a calamity may be a blessing for the patient.
وجعلنا نومكم سباتاً: And We Made Your Sleep a Rest
ذكر الله النوم والليل من نعمه: راحة ونقط: Allah mentions sleep and night among His favours: rest and a cessation of movement. Al-Sa'di and Ibn Kathir explained that bodies tire from continuous movement, so Allah made sleep a rest for them.
ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه: Whoever Relies upon Allah, He Is Sufficient for Him
وعد الله من يتوكل عليه بأن يكفيه. وبيّن: Allah promised that whoever relies on Him will find Him sufficient. Al-Sa'di explained trust: relying on Allah in bringing what benefits and repelling what harms, with confidence in His facilitation; it is among the causes of the heart's stillness.
ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يري: Allah Does Not Intend to Place You in Difficulty but to Purify You
ختم الله آية الوضوء والغسل والتيمم بأنه: Allah closed the verse of wudu, ghusl and tayammum by saying that He does not want hardship but wants to purify His servants and complete His favour. Al-Sa'di counted this among the rulings drawn from the verse: legislation is mercy.
سمّى الله المحيض أذى وأمر باعتزال النساء: Allah called menstruation an impurity and commanded that women be kept apart during it until they are clean. Al-Sa'di explained that since it is an impurity it is wise for Allah to forbid His servants from it, and that the prohibition is kindness to them.
فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المط: In It Are Men Who Love to Purify Themselves, and Allah Loves Those Who Purify Themselves
مدح الله أهل قباء الذين يحبون التطهر وأخ: Allah praised the people of Quba who love to be purified and said that He loves those who purify themselves. Al-Sa'di explained that purity is both moral and physical: freeing oneself from shirk and base characters, and removing impurities and lifting states of impurity.
من أوائل ما نزل: الأمر بتطهير الثياب. وذ: Among the first things revealed: the command to purify clothing. Al-Sa'di mentioned two possibilities: that it means all one's deeds, or the familiar garments, which are to be cleansed of impurities at all times.
وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهوراً: And We Sent Down from the Sky Pure Water
ذكر الله أنه أنزل من السماء ماءً طهوراً،: Allah mentioned that He sent down pure water from the sky, and al-Sa'di explained that it purifies from ritual impurity and filth, that it has blessing, and that it is a provision for people and livestock.
والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين: Mothers Shall Nurse Their Children for Two Complete Years
جعل الله مدة الرضاعة الكاملة حولين لمن أ: Allah made the full nursing period two years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing. Al-Sa'di explained that when two years are complete for the infant, his nursing is complete, and the milk after that becomes like other foods.
وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهراً: And His Bearing and His Weaning Are Thirty Months
ذكر الله ما تحمّلته الأم من الحمل والولا: Allah mentioned what the mother bore of pregnancy, childbirth and nursing, and made "his bearing and his weaning" thirty months. Al-Sa'di explained that pregnancy is about nine months and the rest is for nursing; this is the usual case.
حملته أمه وهناً على وهن: His Mother Carried Him in Weakness upon Weakness
وصّى الله الإنسان بوالديه وذكر ما تحمّلت: Allah enjoined man to be good to his parents and mentioned what the mother bore: "weakness upon weakness" and weaning in two years. Al-Sa'di explained it as successive hardship: morning sickness, illness, weakness and heaviness, then the pain of delivery.
الذي خَلَقَني فهو يهديني}: هو [المنْفَرِ: He alone is the One Who made creation and guidance, and He singled out some of the necessities, saying: "And it is He Who feeds me and gives me drink, and when I am ill, it is He Who heals me, and Who causes me to die then gives me life, and Who, I hope, will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgement". So He alone is unique in that, and so He alone must be singled out for worship and obedience, and these idols must be left, which create not and guide not, make no one ill and heal no one …
مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلاَّ أَنْزَ: Allah did not send down a disease except that He sent down a cure for it.
لِكُلِّ دَاءٍ دَوَاءٌ فَإِذَا أُصِيبَ دَ: Every disease has a cure; when the cure matches the disease, it heals by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
فقيل له: {اركُضۡ برِجۡلِكَ}؛ أي: اضربِ ا: And it was said to him: "Strike with your foot", that is, strike the earth with it so that a spring may gush forth for you from which you may wash and drink, and the harm and affliction will leave you. He did so, the harm left him, and Allah the Exalted healed him.
ثم لما أرسله معهم؛ وصَّاهم إذا هم قدموا: He then enjoined them, when they reached Egypt, not to enter "by one gate but enter by different gates": he feared the evil eye for them because of their large number and fine appearance, as sons of one man, and this is a means, "and I cannot avail you at all against Allah", for what is decreed must come to pass. "The decision is only for Allah", that is, the judgement is His judgement and the command is His command, so what He has decreed and judged must happen. "In Him I put my trust", that is, I relied on Allah and not on the means I advised you to take.
تَدَاوَوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَضَعْ د: Seek treatment, for Allah has not placed a disease except that He placed a cure for it—or he said "a remedy"—except for one disease." They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said, "Old age.
والإلقاء باليد إلى التهلكة يرجع إلى أمري: Throwing oneself by one's own hand into destruction comes down to two matters: leaving what the servant was commanded when leaving it causes or nearly causes the destruction of the body or the soul, and doing what is a cause that leads to the ruin of the self or the soul. Many things fall under that. Among them is leaving jihad in the way of Allah, or spending on it, which brings about the domination of enemies; and among them is a person's exposing himself to danger in fighting, or a frightening journey, or a place of beasts or snakes, or climbing a tree or a dangerous building, or going under something dangerous and the like; this and the like is one who has thrown himself by his own hand into destruction
فَإِنَّ لِجَسَدِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَإِ: for your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, your wife has a right over you, and your visitor has a right over you.
نِعْمَتَانِ مَغْبُونٌ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌ م: There are two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and free time.
ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم}؛ أي: لا يقتل بعضكم بع: "and do not kill yourselves", that is, let not some of you kill others, nor let a person kill himself, and that includes throwing oneself into destruction and committing dangerous acts that lead to ruin and destruction
إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ بِالطَّاعُونِ بِأَرْضٍ: If you hear of the plague in a land, do not enter it; and if it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave it.
لاَ يُورِدُ مُمْرِضٌ عَلَى مُصِحٍّ: A person with sick camels must not bring them to those that are healthy.
في خلق هذه النَّحلة الصغيرة، التي هداها: in the creation of this little bee, which Allah guided with this wonderful guidance, and made easy for it the pastures, then its return to the homes it has prepared by Allah's teaching and guidance to it, then there comes out of its belly this delicious honey, of different colours according to the difference of its land and pastures; in it is healing for people from many diseases. So this is a proof of the perfection of Allah's care and the fullness of His kindness to His servants, and that He is the One besides Whom none should be loved, and none else should be called upon.
الثَّانِيَةُ- قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُخْتَ: He means its kinds: red, white and yellow, solid and liquid; the mother is one while the offspring differ, which is a proof that the Power varied it according to the variety of the food, just as its taste differs according to the difference of the pastures; and from this sense is the saying of Zaynab to the Prophet, peace be upon him, "Its bees fed on the urfut", when she likened its smell to the smell of maghafir.
الشِّفَاءُ فِي ثَلاَثَةٍ شَرْبَةِ عَسَلٍ: Healing is in three: a drink of honey, the cupper's incision, and cauterisation by fire; and I forbid my community from cauterisation.
فَقَالَ أَخِي يَشْتَكِي بَطْنَهُ. فَقَال: He said, "My brother complains of his stomach." He said, "Give him honey to drink." Then he came a second time and he said, "Give him honey to drink." Then he came and said, "I did." He said, "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's stomach has lied. Give him honey to drink." So he gave it to him and he recovered.
الثَّالِثَةُ- قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿فِيهِ: The pronoun refers to honey, said the majority, that is, in honey there is healing for people. And it is related from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Farra and Ibn Kaysan that the pronoun refers to the Quran, that is, in the Quran there is healing. al-Nahhas said: this is a good view, or in what We have narrated to you of the signs and proofs there is healing for people. And it was said: honey has healing in it, and this view is also clear, because most of the drinks and electuaries with which treatment is given originate from honey.
وَقَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ: إِنَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى: A group said: that is specific and does not imply generality for every illness and every person; rather it is a report that it heals as other medicines heal, in some cases and in one condition rather than another. The benefit of the verse is its report that it is a medicine, since healing by it was frequent and it became a mixture and an aid to medicines in drinks and electuaries. And this is not the first expression to be specified, for the Quran is full of it, and in the language of the Arabs the general often comes with the sense of the specific and the specific with the sense of the general. And among what indicates that it is not general is that "healing" is indefinite in an affirmative context, and there is no generality in it by agreement of the people of the language, the verifying scholars and those who differ among the scholars of the principles.
ثُمَّ قِيلَ: فِي قِلَّةِ الْأَكْلِ مَنَا: Then it was said: in eating little there are many benefits, among them that a man is healthier in body, better in memory, keener in understanding, less in sleep and lighter in spirit. And in eating much there is the heaviness of the stomach and the foulness of indigestion, and various diseases arise from it, so he needs more treatment than the one who eats little needs.
مَا مَلأَ آدَمِيٌّ وِعَاءً شَرًّا مِنْ ب: The son of Adam fills no vessel worse than his stomach. It is enough for the son of Adam to have a few morsels to keep his back straight; and if the self of the son of Adam overcomes him, then a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breath.
هذا خطاب للناس كلهم مؤمنهم وكافرهم، فامت: This is an address to all people, believer and disbeliever, and He reminded them of His favour by commanding them to eat of all that is in the earth of grains, fruits, produce and animals, while it is "lawful", that is, permitted for you to take, not by usurpation or theft or by a forbidden transaction or by a forbidden means or aiding something forbidden, "and good", that is, not foul, like carrion, blood, pork and all foul things. So in this verse is proof that the basic rule for things is permissibility, in eating and in benefit, and that the forbidden is of two kinds: either forbidden in itself, which is the foul that is the opposite of the good, or forbidden for something incidental, which is forbidden because a right of Allah or of His servants attaches to it, and it is the opposite of the lawful.
أي: {إنَّ لكُم في الأنعام}: التي سخَّرها: that is, "indeed, for you in the livestock" which Allah has subjected for your benefit "is a lesson" by which you may infer the perfection of Allah's power and the breadth of His kindness, in that He gave you drink from their bellies, which contain dung and blood, and brought out from between that milk, pure of impurity, palatable for those who drink, for its pleasantness and because it quenches and nourishes. Is this other than divine power and not natural matters? What in nature turns the fodder that the animal eats and the water, sweet and salty, that it drinks into pure milk, pleasant to drink?
قَالَ عُلَمَاؤُنَا: فَكَيْفَ لَا يَكُونُ: Our scholars said: how could it not be so, when it is the first thing a human is nourished by and bodies grow through, so it is a food free of defects by which the bodies are sustained, and Allah made it a sign for Jibril of the guidance of this community, which is the best of communities, for he said in the Sahih: "Jibril came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibril said to me: you chose the natural way; had you chosen wine, your community would have gone astray".
أي: أولم ينظُر هؤلاء الذين كفروا بربِّهم: that is, have those who disbelieved in their Lord and denied sincerity to Him in worship not seen what shows them, as a matter of observation, that He is the praiseworthy, generous Lord, the One worshipped, as they observe the heaven and the earth and find them "closed up": this one has no cloud or rain, and that one is barren and dead, with no vegetation, "then We opened them", the heaven with rain and the earth with plants. Is it not He Who brought into being the cloud in the sky after the air was clear with not a wisp in it, and deposited in it abundant water, then drove it to a dead land whose horizons had grown dusty and from which water was withheld, and sent rain on it, and it stirred, swelled and grew every kind of beautiful plant, varied in kinds, many in benefits …

أعرضنا عن مواضع شاع ذكرها لضعف صلتها بال: We left out points that are often cited but whose link to the text is weak or whose scientific fact is not settled, among them: linking "a lying, sinning forelock" to the frontal lobe, linking the exchange of skins to pain receptors, linking "the mountains pass like clouds" to the earth's rotation, and everything built on counts of letters and words. The safer method is to say only what is scientifically established and what the language and exegesis support.
القرآن كتاب هداية، وآياته الكونية دعوة إ: The Quran is a book of guidance, and its cosmic verses are an invitation to reflect; it is not a book of experimental science. So here we keep to what science has settled with confidence, the text is not loaded onto a hypothesis that may change, a word is not taken out of its meaning in Arabic, and the contemporary understanding is shown alongside the exegetes' explanation and never placed above it. Al-Shatibi in "al-Muwafaqat" was cautious about reading the Quran as containing sciences the Arabs did not know, Ibn Ashur gave a detailed treatment in the fourth introduction of "al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir", and others went further; so we state each theme's grade. The verse texts follow the Madinah mushaf wording and script, and the exegetes' words and hadiths are excerpted verbatim from their books bundled in Mishkat; the mark "…" shows that what lies between excerpts was omitted. "What science says today" is our own summary of facts established in the references cited, not a quotation from any one scholar. This section is for reflection and study and is not a fatwa.
